The tooth fairy had finally come! She was wearing a pink dress and had a sparkly wand in her hand. Sammy smiled at her. She waved her wand and a coin appeared. It was Sammy's tooth fairy reward! She left the coin on his bed and flew away.

Then Sammy was happy. He knew the tooth fairy would come back the next time one of his teeth came out. And he knew that he would be given a reward every time. Sammy was smart, and he always remembered to be kind and to take care of his teeth.

"Hello, Mr. Skeleton," Jack said. "Can I count your bones?"

The skeleton laughed and said, "Sure, little one. But be careful, I have a wise secret to tell you."

Jack counted the bones one by one. "There are 206 bones in your body, Mr. Skeleton!" he exclaimed.

"Very good, Jack," the skeleton said. "Now, my wise secret is this: always count your blessings, not your bones."

Jack didn't understand what the skeleton meant, but he remembered the wise words. Later that day, Jack's mom made his favorite cookies. Jack counted how many cookies he got and said, "I have so many blessings!"

Sara and Ben say, "We did. Thank you for the ride. And the silly hats."

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is black and brown, and has a loud bark. Ben and Mia are nervous. They do not like big dogs. They think the dog will chase them and bite them.

"Mom, Dad, look! A big dog!" Ben says.

"Shh, Ben, do not yell. The dog will hear you," Mom says.

"Let's go the other way. Maybe the dog will not see us," Dad says.

"Help, help! The dog is coming!" Mia says.

"Stay close to us, Mia. The dog will not hurt you," Dad says.

"Mom, what do we do?" Ben says.

"Look, Ben, there is a twist in the path. Maybe we can hide behind the trees," Mom says.

But then, they hear another sound. They hear a whistle and a voice.

"Rex, Rex, come here, boy! Where are you, Rex?" the voice says.

They open their eyes and peek from behind the tree. They see a man with a leash and a hat. He is looking for the dog.

"Is that the dog's owner?" Mia says.

They watch as the man finds the dog and puts the leash on him. He pets the dog and talks to him.

"Good boy, Rex. You are a good dog. But you cannot run away from me. You scared those people. You have to be nice to them," the man says.

He sees Ben and Mia behind the tree. He smiles and waves at them.

"Hello, kids. I'm sorry about Rex. He is a friendly dog, but he gets excited sometimes. He likes to jog, too. Do you want to say hi to him?" the man says.

Ben and Mia look at Mom and Dad. Mom and Dad nod and smile. They are not nervous anymore.

Ben and Mia come out from behind the tree. They walk slowly to the man and the dog. The dog wags his tail and licks their hands. He is soft and warm.

The man laughs and says, "That's OK, kids. Rex is sorry, too. He likes to make new friends. Maybe next time, we can jog together. What do you say, Rex?"

The dog barks and nods. He likes the idea.

Ben and Mia smile and say, "Maybe, maybe. But not today. Today, we have to go home. Bye, Rex. Bye, man."

They wave goodbye to the man and the dog. They jog back to Mom and Dad. They are happy and proud.

They all ran to the castle. They pretended to be kings and queens, knights and princesses. They had a lot of fun.

But then, the sky became dark and gloomy. They heard thunder and saw lightning. They felt raindrops on their heads.

"Oh no!" Tom said. "It is going to rain!"

"Our castle!" Anna said. "It will get wet and break!"

They were sad. They did not want to lose their castle.

"Quick!" Sam said. "Let's go to the shelter!"

He pointed to a big tree nearby. It had thick branches and leaves.

"Good idea!" Lily said. "Let's go!"

They grabbed their toys and ran to the tree. They sat under it and waited for the rain to stop.

They looked at their castle. It was still standing, but it looked wet and sad.

They hoped it would not fall down.

They hugged each other and smiled.

They still had their friends. And they could always make another castle.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big sign with a map on it. The map showed all the places in the park, like the swings, the slide, the pond and the trees.

"Look, Ben, this is a map. It helps us find our way," Sara said. She pointed to the map and explained what each picture meant.

Ben nodded. He liked the map. He wanted to see all the places on it. He took Sara's hand and said, "Let's go to the pond. I want to see the ducks."

They followed the map and walked to the pond. They saw some ducks swimming and quacking. They also saw some bread on the ground. Ben picked up a piece and threw it to the ducks.

"Ben, don't do that!" Sara said. "That bread is not good for the ducks. It can make them sick."

Ben looked confused. He said, "But they like it. They eat it."

Sara shook her head. She said, "They eat it because they are hungry, but it is not the right food for them. They need seeds and plants and bugs. That is what they eat in nature. The bread is too soft and sticky. It can hurt their stomachs and their feathers."

Ben felt sorry. He did not want to hurt the ducks. He said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I did not know that. How can we help them?"

Sara smiled. She said, "We can help them by leaving them alone. They can find their own food in the pond. And we can tell other people not to feed them bread. We can explain why it is bad for them."

Ben nodded. He said, "OK, Sara. You are smart. You know a lot of things. Thank you for explaining to me."

Sara hugged Ben. She said, "You are welcome, Ben. You are kind. You care about the ducks. Thank you for listening to me."

They left the pond and went to see the other places on the map. They had fun and learned a lot.

The moral value of the story is: We should respect and protect the animals and their habitats. We should also listen and learn from each other.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but her favorite was a big red car. She liked to zoom it around the room and make loud noises.

One day, her mom told her it was time to go to bed. Lily did not want to go to bed. She wanted to play with her car some more. She said, "No, mom, I want to play!"

Her mom said, "Lily, you have to go to bed. It is late and you need to sleep. You can play with your car tomorrow."

Lily did not listen. She ran away from her mom and hid under the table with her car. She thought her mom would not find her there.

But her mom was not happy. She looked for Lily and saw her under the table. She said, "Lily, come out of there. You are being naughty. You have to go to bed now."

Lily tried to resist. She said, "No, mom, I want to stay here!"

Her mom said, "Lily, if you don't come out, I will set the alarm. The alarm will make a loud noise and scare you. Do you want that?"

Lily did not like the alarm. The alarm was scary. It made a beep beep beep sound that hurt her ears. She did not want to hear the alarm.

She thought for a moment. She realized that her mom was right. She needed to go to bed. She needed to sleep. She could play with her car tomorrow.

She said, "Sorry, mom. I will go to bed. I don't want the alarm."

Her mom smiled. She said, "That's a good girl. I love you, Lily. Come on, let's go to bed."

Lily came out of the table. She gave her mom a hug. She said, "I love you, mom. Good night."

She took her car with her and put it on her bedside. She went to bed and fell asleep.

The moral of the story is: You should listen to your mom and go to bed when she tells you. If you don't, you might get scared by the alarm. It is better to be obedient and sleep well than to be naughty and stay up late.

Lily loved to imagine. She imagined she was a princess, a pirate, a fairy, or anything she wanted. She had a big box of costumes and toys to help her pretend. But today, she was bored. She had played with everything in her box, and it was a gloomy day outside. She wished she had something new and exciting to play with.

She decided to explore the attic. She climbed the stairs and opened the door. It was dark and dusty, and full of old things. She saw a trunk in the corner. She wondered what was inside. She pulled the trunk to the window and opened the lid. She gasped. It was full of gold! Shiny, sparkly, golden coins and jewels. She felt like she had found a treasure.

She grabbed a handful of gold and put it in her pocket. She wanted to show it to her mom and dad. She ran down the stairs, but she tripped and fell. The gold flew out of her pocket and rolled all over the floor. She heard a voice behind her.

"What are you doing, Lily?" It was her dad. He looked angry.

"I found gold, daddy! Look!" She pointed to the floor.

"That's not gold, Lily. That's fake. It's just plastic and glitter. It's from an old Halloween costume. You shouldn't have taken it. And you shouldn't have gone to the attic. It's not safe. You could have hurt yourself."

Lily felt sad and ashamed. She had imagined she had found something wonderful, but it was only a lie. She had broken the rules and made a mess. She started to cry.

"I'm sorry, daddy. I just wanted to have fun. I was bored."

Her dad sighed and hugged her.

"I know, Lily. I know. But you have to be careful and listen to me. I don't want you to get in trouble or get hurt. Come on, let's clean up this mess and go downstairs. Maybe we can find something else to play with. Something real."

Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She helped her dad pick up the fake gold and put it back in the trunk. She learned her lesson. She realized that imagining was fun, but not when it made her do bad things. She decided to use her imagination for good, not for greed. She hoped her dad would forgive her and play with her. She still loved to imagine, but she also loved her dad.

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park, read books, and share toys. One day, they went to the pool with their moms. Lily wore a lovely pink sweater over her swimsuit. Max wore a blue sweater over his swimsuit.

"Look, Lily, the water is so shiny and cool!" Max said. "Let's swim and splash!"

"Okay, Max, but first I have to take off my sweater. It is too warm for the pool," Lily said. She put her sweater on a chair near the pool.

Max did not take off his sweater. He was in a hurry to swim. He jumped into the water with his sweater on. He felt wet and heavy. He could not swim well. He started to sink.

"Help, help!" Max cried. "I can't swim!"

Lily heard Max's cry. She quickly swam to him and grabbed his hand. She pulled him to the edge of the pool. She helped him get out of the water.

"Max, are you okay?" Lily asked. She was worried and scared.

"I'm okay, Lily, thank you for saving me," Max said. He was shivering and coughing. He looked at his sweater. It was soaked and dripping.

"Max, why did you swim with your sweater on?" Lily asked. "You know you have to take it off before you swim."

"I was too excited to swim. I forgot to take it off. I was silly and careless," Max said. He felt sorry and ashamed.

"Lily, I'm sorry I ruined your lovely sweater. It is all wet and dirty now," Max said. He pointed to Lily's sweater on the chair. It had fallen on the ground and was covered with mud and leaves.

"That's okay, Max. My sweater can be washed and dried. I'm just glad you are safe and sound. You are more important than my sweater," Lily said. She hugged Max and smiled.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. I learned my lesson. Next time, I will take off my sweater before I swim. And I will be more careful and listen to my mom," Max said. He hugged Lily back and smiled.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of friendship, safety, and responsibility. It shows that friends should help each other in times of trouble, that swimming with clothes on is dangerous, and that listening to parents is wise.

"What flavor do you want?" the man in the truck said.

"I want chocolate!" Jen said.

"I want strawberry!" Sam said.

The man gave them their ice cream cones and they paid him with their coins. They thanked him and skipped away to a bench.

They licked their ice cream and smiled. It was cold and sweet and yummy.

But then, Sam made a face. His ice cream tasted weird. It was not strawberry. It was something else.

"Yuck! What is this?" he said.

"Maybe it's mint?" she said.

She took a bite of his ice cream to see. She spit it out right away. It was not mint. It was something else.

"Yuck! What is this?" she said.

They looked at the truck. The sign said "Ice Cream", but under it, there was another sign that said "Try our new flavor: Pickle!"

They had been tricked. The man in the truck had given them pickle ice cream instead of strawberry.

They threw their cones in the trash and ran away. They did not like pickle ice cream. It was cold and sour and yucky.

They decided to never buy ice cream from that truck again. They learned to always check the flavor before they eat.

But then, something bad happened. Lily slid down too fast and lost her grip on Rosie. Rosie flew out of her arms and landed on the ground. Lily heard a loud crack. She ran to Rosie and saw that her head was broken. She started to cry and scream. Mommy came to her and tried to comfort her. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Rosie is broken. We can try to fix her later, okay?"

Lily was very sad and angry. She did not want to fix Rosie. She wanted Rosie to be whole and happy. She said, "No, Mommy. Rosie is gone. She is not my doll anymore. She is a nightmare." She threw Rosie away and ran to the car. Mommy followed her and picked up Rosie. She felt sorry for Lily and Rosie.

That night, Lily did not want to sleep. She did not want to see Rosie in her dreams. She did not want to hug any other doll. She only wanted Rosie back. She lay in her bed and cried. Mommy came to her and said, "Lily, I know you are hurt. But Rosie is still your doll. She still loves you. And I love you too. Can I give you a hug?" Lily looked at Mommy and saw that she was holding Rosie. Rosie had a bandage around her head and a new smile on her face. Mommy had fixed her. Lily felt a warm feeling in her heart. She said, "Mommy, thank you. Can I hug Rosie too?" Mommy said, "Of course, Lily. Here, take her. She missed you." Lily took Rosie and hugged her. She said, "Rosie, I'm sorry. I love you. You are not a nightmare. You are my best friend." Rosie did not say anything, but Lily felt that she understood. Lily smiled and kissed Rosie. She said, "Good night, Rosie. Good night, Mommy." Mommy said, "Good night, Lily. Good night, Rosie. Sweet dreams." She tucked them in and turned off the light. Lily and Rosie fell asleep, happy and safe.

Ben and Lily were playing in the sandbox. They had shovels and buckets and made castles and tunnels. They were having fun, but they were also getting filthy. Their hands and clothes were covered in sand and dirt.

"Look, Mommy is calling us," Lily said. "It's time for lunch."

Ben frowned. He did not want to stop playing. He liked the sandbox. He did not like lunch. Lunch was boring and yucky.

"Can we play some more?" he asked Lily.

Lily shook her head. "No, we have to go. Mommy will be mad if we don't. And we have to wash our hands and faces. We are filthy."

Ben sighed. He followed Lily to the house. He wished he could stay in the sandbox. He wished he could imagine a different lunch. A lunch that was not boring and yucky. A lunch that was fun and yummy.

He imagined a lunch that was made of sand and dirt. He imagined that he could eat his castles and tunnels. He imagined that they tasted like candy and ice cream. He imagined that Lily would eat them with him. He imagined that Mommy would not be mad. He imagined that they would all laugh and smile.

He smiled as he imagined his lunch. He did not notice that Mommy was holding a plate of sandwiches and fruit. He did not notice that Lily was saying, "Look, Ben, we have a nice lunch. It's not boring and yucky. It's good and healthy."

He did not notice until he took a bite of his sandwich. He realized that it was not sand and dirt. He realized that it was bread and cheese. He realized that it was not candy and ice cream. He realized that it was lunch.

He spat out his sandwich. He made a face. He said, "Yuck! I don't like this lunch. I want my sand and dirt lunch. I want my candy and ice cream lunch."

Mommy and Lily looked at him. They did not understand. They did not know what he was imagining. They did not know why he was being silly. They did not know what to say.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play together. They had a big box that they used as a sail boat. They cut out a sail from a white sheet and tied it to a stick. They also drew windows and doors on the box with crayons.

One day, they decided to sail to a faraway island. They put some toys and snacks in their boat and pushed it to the backyard. They pretended that the grass was the sea and the flowers were fish. They sang songs and waved to their parents who watched them from the window.

"Look, Lily, there is the island!" Tom said, pointing to a big tree. "It has lovely green leaves and colorful birds. Let's go and explore it."

"OK, Tom, but we have to be careful. There might be pirates or wild animals there." Lily said, holding Tom's hand.

They got out of their boat and walked to the tree. They saw a swing, a slide and a sandbox under the branches. They were very happy and played with them for a long time. They also shared their snacks and gave some to the birds.

"This is the best island ever!" Tom said, smiling. "I'm glad we came here."

"Me too, Tom. And I'm glad we are friends." Lily said, hugging him. "Can we include the birds as our friends too?"

"Of course, Lily. The more friends, the merrier." Tom said, nodding. "Let's sail back home and tell our parents about our adventure."

They got back in their boat and sailed home. They had a lovely day and a lot of fun. They thanked their parents for letting them play and promised to sail again soon.

Lily liked to knit with her yarn. She had many colors of yarn and she made hats and scarves for her dolls. She learned to knit from her grandma, who was very patient and kind.

One day, Lily wanted to knit a big blanket for her teddy bear. She asked her grandma for help. "Grandma, can you show me how to knit a big blanket?" she said.

"Of course, my dear," her grandma said. "But you need a lot of yarn and a lot of time. Knitting a big blanket is not easy. You have to be patient and careful."

Lily nodded. She wanted to make a nice blanket for her teddy bear. She followed her grandma to the closet, where she kept her yarn. She picked a soft pink yarn and a fluffy white yarn. She thought they would look pretty together.

Her grandma gave her a big pair of needles and showed her how to cast on. "You have to make a loop with the yarn and put it on the needle," she said. "Then you have to pull the yarn and make another loop. You have to do this many times until you have enough loops for your blanket."

Lily tried to do what her grandma said. She made a loop with the yarn and put it on the needle. Then she pulled the yarn and made another loop. She did this again and again. She counted the loops. She had ten loops. She was proud of herself.

"Very good, Lily," her grandma said. "Now you have to knit the loops. You have to take the other needle and put it through the first loop. Then you have to wrap the yarn around the needle and pull it through the loop. Then you have to slide the loop off the needle. You have to do this for every loop."

Lily tried to do what her grandma said. She took the other needle and put it through the first loop. Then she wrapped the yarn around the needle and pulled it through the loop. Then she slid the loop off the needle. She did this for every loop. She had one row of stitches. She was happy.

"Very good, Lily," her grandma said. "Now you have to turn your work and do the same thing for the next row. You have to keep doing this until your blanket is big enough for your teddy bear. But remember, you have to stretch the yarn a little bit before you wrap it around the needle. If you don't stretch the yarn, your blanket will be too tight and hard. If you stretch the yarn too much, your blanket will be too loose and holey. You have to stretch the yarn just right."

Lily nodded. She wanted to make a perfect blanket for her teddy bear. She turned her work and did the same thing for the next row. She stretched the yarn a little bit before she wrapped it around the needle. She did this for every row. She knitted and knitted and knitted. She used all the pink yarn and all the white yarn. She made a big blanket for her teddy bear. She was very proud of herself.

"Very good, Lily," her grandma said. "You did a wonderful job. Your blanket is beautiful and soft and warm. Your teddy bear will love it. You are a very good knitter. You are very patient and careful."

Lily smiled. She hugged her grandma and thanked her for her help. She wrapped her blanket around her teddy bear and cuddled with him. She was very happy. She loved her grandma and her teddy bear and her yarn.

"Can I play with the toys, grandma?" Tom asked.

"Of course, my dear. But first, let's help your mom unpack your bags. She has some medicine for me that I need to take every day," grandma said.

Tom and his mom followed grandma to her bedroom, where they put their bags on the bed. Tom helped his mom open the bags and take out the clothes and the medicine. He saw a small bottle with a label that said "grandma's medicine". He was curious and wanted to know what it was.

"What is this, mom?" Tom asked, holding the bottle.

"That's grandma's medicine, Tom. She has to take it every day to make her feel better. It helps her heart beat well and her blood flow well. It's very important that she doesn't miss it or take too much of it," mom explained.

Tom nodded and gave the bottle to his mom. He understood that grandma needed the medicine to stay healthy and happy. He wanted to help her remember to take it.

"Can I give grandma her medicine, mom?" Tom asked.

"Sure, Tom. But you have to be very careful and follow the instructions. You have to give her one spoonful of the medicine with some water, and only when it's time. You can't give her more or less than that, or it could make her sick. Do you understand?" mom said.

Tom nodded again and took the bottle and a spoon. He felt proud and responsible. He wanted to be a good grandson and a good helper.

"Come on, grandma. Let's go to the kitchen and get some water. I'll give you your medicine," Tom said.

"Thank you, Tom. You're such a sweet boy. But be careful, don't spill the medicine. It's very fierce and it tastes bad," grandma said.

Tom and grandma walked to the kitchen, holding hands. Tom was careful not to spill the medicine. He poured some water in a glass and gave it to grandma. Then he measured one spoonful of the medicine and gave it to grandma too.

"Here you go, grandma. Drink this and you'll feel better," Tom said.

Grandma smiled and drank the medicine. She made a face and said, "Yuck! That's very fierce. But thank you, Tom. You're a very good helper. I love you very much."

Tom smiled and hugged grandma. He said, "I love you too, grandma. And I'm glad you're feeling better."

She did not see the tiny light that came closer and closer to her. It was a real fairy who heard Lily's voice and wanted to meet her. The fairy was bald, because she had lost her hair in a storm. She felt sad and lonely.

"Hello, I am Fairy Nix. I can make stars shine and rainbows appear. Do you want to be my friend?" the fairy said in a soft voice.

Lily was surprised and happy. She saw the fairy and smiled. She did not mind that the fairy was bald. She thought she was beautiful and kind.

"Hello, I am Lily. I can make stories and songs. I want to be your friend!" Lily said in a loud voice.

The fairy and the doll flew to Lily's hand. They hugged and laughed. They became friends and played together. They made flowers, animals, stars and rainbows. They made stories and songs. They had fun and were happy.

Lily and Tom were playing in the bathroom. They liked to pretend they were grown-ups. Lily found a razor on the sink. It was shiny and modern. She wanted to try it.

"Look, Tom, I found a razor. I can shave like Daddy!" she said.

"No, Lily, don't touch it! It is sharp and dangerous. You can hurt yourself!" Tom said.

But Lily did not listen. She took the razor and put it on her cheek. She felt a sting and saw blood. She started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts, Tom, it hurts!" she repeated.

Tom ran to get Mommy. He was scared and sorry. He wished he had stopped Lily.

Mommy came and saw what happened. She was angry and worried. She took the razor away and cleaned Lily's wound. She put a band-aid on it and hugged her.

"Lily, you were very naughty and foolish. You should never play with razors. They are not toys. They are for grown-ups only. Do you understand?" she said.

"Yes, Mommy, I understand. I'm sorry, Mommy. I won't do it again." Lily said.

Mommy kissed her and said, "I love you, Lily, but you have to be careful and listen to Tom. He was trying to help you. Can you say sorry to him too?"

Lily looked at Tom. He was still sad and scared. She felt bad. She said, "Sorry, Tom. You were right. I should have listened to you. Can we still be friends?"

Tom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. We are always friends. I love you, Lily. But please don't play with razors again."

They hugged and said, "We love you, Mommy."

Mommy smiled and said, "I love you too, my sweet children. Now let's go and have some cookies and milk."

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big tree with many green olives that they could pick and eat. One day, they saw an old bird sitting on a branch. The bird looked tired and sad.

"Hello, bird," Ben said. "Why are you so old and sad?"

The bird looked at Ben and said, "I have flown a long way from my home. I have no friends or family here. I am lonely and hungry."

Lily felt sorry for the bird. She said, "We can be your friends, bird. And we can share our olives with you. They are yummy and good for you."

The bird smiled and said, "Thank you, twins. You are very kind and sweet. Can I rest here for a while?"

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, bird. You can rest here as long as you want. We will keep you company and play with you."

The bird was happy and grateful. He ate some olives and rested on the branch. He felt warm and safe. He sang a beautiful song for Ben and Lily. They clapped and cheered.

The twins and the bird became good friends. They played and talked every day. The bird told them stories of his home and his travels. Ben and Lily learned many new things from him. They also taught him some of their games and songs. They had a lot of fun together.

The old bird was not sad anymore. He was glad he had met Ben and Lily. He decided to stay with them in the garden. He said, "You are the best friends I ever had. You have made me happy and young again."

"What is that?" asked the mouse.

"It is a cave," said the bunny. "Maybe there is something inside."

"Let's go and see," said the mouse. "Maybe we can find a treasure."

They hopped into the cave. It was cold and quiet. They saw some shiny rocks and some bones. They heard a growl.

"Who is there?" asked a voice. It was loud and scary.

The bunny and the mouse were afraid. They saw a big bear. He had sharp teeth and claws. He was angry.

"This is my cave," he said. "Go away or I will eat you."

The bunny and the mouse did not want to be eaten. They ran and hopped as fast as they could. They got out of the cave and back to the forest.

"That was a bad idea," said the mouse.

"Yes, it was," said the bunny. "The cave was too mysterious and dangerous. Let's never go there again."

They hugged each other and went to find a safer place to play.

Anna and Ben nod their heads. They understand. They are sorry. They want to make Mom happy. They kneel on the floor and start to pick up their toys and clothes. They put them in their boxes and drawers. They say sorry to Mom again.

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to play together. They had many toys, but they did not like to share them. They always said, "This is mine, you cannot have it." They did not let other children join their games.

One day, a new girl came to their school. Her name was Mia. She had no toys, but she had a big smile. She asked Lily and Sam if she could play with them. But they said, "No, you cannot. Go away."

Mia felt sad, but she did not give up. She looked around and saw a big tree. She climbed the tree and found a bird's nest. She saw three eggs in the nest. She said, "Hello, little birds. Can I join you?" The birds did not answer, but they did not mind.

Lily and Sam saw Mia in the tree. They were curious. They asked, "What are you doing up there?" Mia said, "I am playing with the birds. They are my friends. They have eggs. They are very pretty."

Lily and Sam wanted to see the eggs. They said, "Can we join you?" Mia said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be gentle and quiet. The eggs are not birds yet. They need time and love to grow."

Lily and Sam climbed the tree and saw the eggs. They were amazed. They said, "Wow, they are so beautiful. Can we touch them?" Mia said, "Yes, but only with one finger. And do not shake them. They are very fragile."

Lily and Sam touched the eggs with one finger. They felt warm and smooth. They said, "They are so nice. Thank you for letting us join you, Mia. You are very kind."

Mia said, "You are welcome. I am happy to share with you. Sharing is fun. Maybe you can share your toys with me and other children too."

Lily and Sam thought about it. They said, "Yes, you are right. Sharing is fun. We are sorry for being mean to you and other children. We will share our toys with you and other children from now on."

Mia said, "That is great. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now we can all be friends and play together."

The next day, Lily and Sam brought their toys to school. They invited Mia and other children to play with them. They had a lot of fun. They also brought some cookies for everyone. They said, "These are delicious. Do you want some?" Mia and other children said, "Yes, please. Thank you. You are very generous."

They all ate the cookies and enjoyed them. They said, "These are the best cookies ever. You are the best friends ever."

But then, she saw something sad. She saw a fox lying on the ground. It was not moving. It was not breathing. It was dead. Mia felt sorry for the fox. She wanted to help it.

She kissed the fox and walked away with her dad. She felt sad, but also calm. She knew the fox was not alone. She knew the fox was comforted. She knew the fox was loved.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Lily found a big worm and showed it to Max.

"Look, Max, I found a worm! It is long and wiggly. Do you want to touch it?" Lily asked.

Max shook his head. He did not like worms. He thought they were yucky and slimy. He wanted to find something else to play with.

"No, thank you, Lily. I do not want to touch the worm. I want to find a fancy bug. A fancy bug has wings and colors and sparkles. Like a butterfly or a ladybug. They are pretty and fun. Worms are not fancy. They are boring and gross." Max said.

Lily felt sad. She liked the worm. She thought it was interesting and friendly. She did not care if it was not fancy. She wanted to play with it and learn more about it. She did not understand why Max did not like it.

"Max, you are not nice. The worm is a good bug. It helps the plants grow and makes the soil soft. It does not hurt anyone. It is not boring or gross. It is just different. You should not judge a bug by how it looks. You should judge it by how it acts. That is what matters." Lily said.

Max thought about what Lily said. He realized he was being mean and silly. He did not know anything about the worm. He only cared about how it looked. He decided to give the worm a chance. He apologized to Lily and asked if he could touch the worm.

"I am sorry, Lily. You are right. The worm is a good bug. It does not matter if it is not fancy. It matters if it is kind and helpful. Can I touch the worm? Maybe I will like it too." Max said.

Lily smiled and handed the worm to Max. He gently touched it and felt it wriggle in his hand. He was surprised by how soft and smooth it was. He felt curious and happy. He thanked Lily for sharing the worm with him.

"Thank you, Lily. The worm is not so bad. It is actually pretty cool. I am glad you showed it to me. Can we play with it together? Maybe we can find more worms and make a worm house. That would be fun." Max said.

Lily nodded and hugged Max. They put the worm back in the dirt and started to dig for more. They learned to appreciate the worm and other bugs that were not fancy. They had a lot of fun and became better friends.

The moral of the story is: Do not judge a book by its cover. Or a bug by its look. You might miss out on something wonderful.

Lily and Max were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a huge blueberry bush with many ripe and juicy berries. They wanted to pick some and eat them, but they knew they had to ask their moms first.

They ran to their houses and asked their moms if they could have some blueberries. Their moms said yes, but they had to be careful and not remove too many berries from the bush. They also had to share with each other and not be greedy.

Lily and Max agreed and went back to the garden. They each took a small basket and started to pick some berries. They filled their baskets with blueberries and ate some along the way. They were very happy and thanked the blueberry bush for its fruit.

But then, Max saw a very big and shiny blueberry at the top of the bush. He wanted to have it for himself and did not tell Lily. He climbed on the bush and reached for the blueberry. He pulled it hard and removed it from the stem.

But as he did, he also removed a lot of leaves and branches from the bush. The bush shook and made a loud noise. Lily heard it and looked up. She saw Max holding the big blueberry and the bush looking bare and sad.

"Max, what did you do?" Lily asked. "You removed too many berries and hurt the bush. That is not nice. You should have shared with me and left some for the bush."

Max felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he had been greedy and selfish. He apologized to Lily and the bush. He gave the big blueberry to Lily and said he did not want it anymore. He also put some of his berries back on the bush and hoped it would grow again.

Lily forgave Max and hugged him. She said they could still be friends and enjoy the blueberries together. They ate some more berries and then went to their moms to show them their baskets. Their moms were proud of them and said they had learned a valuable lesson.

The moral of the story is: do not be greedy and selfish, but share and care for others and nature.

Lily and Tom run away. They are scared and sorry. They drop the stick and say, "No more honey, please!"

Tommy loved to whistle. He whistled all day long. He whistled when he woke up, when he ate, when he played, and when he went to bed. He whistled so loud that everyone could hear him.

One day, Tommy went to the park with his mom. He saw a vendor with a big cart. The vendor had many things to sell. He had balloons, and candy, and toys, and books. Tommy wanted to buy something from the vendor. He ran to the cart and whistled.

"Hello, little boy," the vendor said. "Do you want to buy something?"

"Yes, please," Tommy said. "I want a balloon."

"OK, here you go," the vendor said. He gave Tommy a red balloon. "That will be one dollar."

Tommy did not have a dollar. He only had a penny. He gave the penny to the vendor and whistled.

"Hey, that's not enough," the vendor said. "You owe me 99 cents."

"I don't have 99 cents," Tommy said. "I only have a penny."

"That's not fair," the vendor said. "You can't take my balloon for a penny. Give it back to me."

"No, it's mine," Tommy said. He held the balloon tight and whistled.

The vendor got angry. He grabbed the balloon from Tommy and popped it with a pin. The balloon made a loud noise and flew away. Tommy was sad. He cried and whistled.

"Stop whistling," the vendor said. "You are a bad boy. You are a thief. Go away from here."

Tommy ran to his mom. He hugged her and whistled.

"Mommy, the vendor was mean to me," Tommy said. "He took my balloon and broke it."

"I'm sorry, Tommy," his mom said. "But you should not take things that you can't pay for. That's wrong. You have to say sorry to the vendor."

Tommy did not want to say sorry. He did not like the vendor. He whistled louder and louder. He whistled so loud that he hurt his throat. He could not whistle anymore. He lost his voice. He was silent.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a gray octopus who lived in the ocean. The octopus had eight arms and loved to swim around and play with his friends. One day, while he was swimming, he saw a fish who looked very sad. The octopus asked the fish what was wrong, and the fish said that he was lost and didn't know how to get home.

The octopus felt sorry for the fish and decided to help him. He split his arms into two groups of four and made a path for the fish to follow. The fish was very happy and thanked the octopus for his kindness. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to help others when they are in need. Even if it means splitting yourself in two to make a path for someone else, it's always worth it to make someone else happy.

Tom was sad that no one wanted to buy his coal. He thought of a plan to make people buy his coal. He lied to the people and said, "This coal is magic! It can make your house warm all day!" Many people believed Tom and bought his coal.

Soon, the people found out that the coal was not magic. They were angry at Tom for lying to them. The people did not trust Tom anymore, and he could not sell anything in the town again.

The moral of the story is: always be honest and do not lie to others.

The spider's friends were having so much fun they started dancing around the cobweb. One of them went crazy and raced around and around in circles. Everyone started laughing, it was so funny!

Suddenly, the spider saw a big light coming in through the window in the attic. It was getting brighter and brighter until she couldn't see. She heard a voice say "What a crazy cobweb!" It was a little girl who had found the spider's party.

The spider said "Hello! Would you like to join the party too?" The little girl smiled and said "Yes, I'd love to!" So the spider and the little girl danced around the cobweb and had lots of fun.

Her mom smiled and explained, "That's because it's made from flexible glass. As it heats up and cools down, it shrinks and expands, so it's always changing size."

Jenna was very impressed. She loved the idea that the jam jar was so flexible. She said, "Wow! That's so cool!" 

The little girl continued to use the jam jar with her toast every day. Even though it kept shrinking and expanding, Jenna loved it just the same. Whenever it changed size, it was always packed full of delicious jam that she had come to love.

But the rabbit shook its head and replied, "No, I don't want to fight".
The bird was a little sad but then it asked, "How about a race then?".
The rabbit was excited and said, "Yes, let's have a race!".
So the bird and the rabbit ran as fast as they could, through the high grass and up the mountainside. Then they rested beneath the big tree and waited for noon.
When the time came they ran as fast as they could once more. Who do you think won the race?
The rabbit did! It ran so fast it arrived at the finishing line just as the sun was reaching noon.
The bird was happy. It said, "Well done rabbit! That was a great race".
The rabbit smiled and said, "Thank you bird! Maybe we can race again tomorrow?".
The bird smiled too and said, "Yes, that would be fun!".
And so their friendship was stronger than ever.

Lila and Ben are twins. They live in a big city with many tall buildings. The buildings are made of steel. Steel is hard and shiny. Lila and Ben like to look at the steel buildings. They think they are modern and cool.

One day, Lila and Ben go to the park with their mom. They want to play on the swings and the slide. But when they get to the park, they see dark clouds in the sky. The clouds are gray and angry. Lila and Ben hear a loud sound. It is thunder. They feel a drop of water on their nose. It is rain.

"Mom, it is raining!" Lila says. "We can't play on the swings and the slide. They are wet and slippery."

"I know, sweetie," Mom says. "But we can still have fun in the rain. We can splash in the puddles and make mud pies. We can sing and dance and laugh. Rain is not bad. It is good. It makes the plants and the flowers grow. It makes the air fresh and clean. It makes the steel buildings sparkle."

"Mom, you are right," Ben says. "Rain is good. It makes the steel buildings sparkle. Can we go and touch them?"

"Sure, why not?" Mom says. "But first, let's put on our raincoats and boots. We don't want to catch a cold."

Lila and Ben put on their raincoats and boots. They hold Mom's hand. They walk to the steel buildings. They touch the steel. It is cold and smooth. They see their reflection in the steel. They smile and wave. They are happy. They like the rain. They like the steel. They like the city.

The bird looked adorable. Lily and Max smiled. They wanted to make the bird fly. They counted to three and pushed the snowball off the snowman's shoulder. "Release!" they shouted.

Anna is sad. She likes her car. She does not want it to stop.

"Maybe we can," Ben says. "Come with me. We can get some oil from the garage."

"We are going to the moon!" said Tom.

Lily laughed. She thought they were very silly. She came out of the bush and said, "You can't go to the moon. It's too far and too cold. And there is no honey there. Only rocks and dust."

Tom and Sue did not like what Lily said. They thought she was very mean. They stuck out their tongues and said, "You are not invited to our wedding. Go away!"

Ben nodded. He wanted to hear the cricket's noise. He leaned closer to the leaf and listened. He heard a soft chirp-chirp-chirp.

"Can you make the same noise, Ben?" Lily asked.

Ben tried to chirp with his mouth. He sounded funny. Lily laughed. The cricket jumped away.

Lily agreed. She did not want to get hurt. She and Ben observed the orange caterpillar as it crawled on the leaf. They wondered what it would become when it grew up. Maybe a butterfly, or a moth, or something else. They decided to come back another day and see.

Ben frowned. He really wanted to feel the soft feathers. He was not afraid of the bird. He took a step closer to the tree.

"Ben, stop!" Lily said. "Listen to me. The bird is not a toy. It is a living thing. It has feelings. How would you like it if someone tried to touch your hair?"

"Okay, Lily, you are smart," Ben said. "I will not touch the bird. But can we watch it for a while? It is so beautiful and funny."

Anna loved to help her dad on the farm. She liked to feed the chickens, pet the cows and watch the sheep. One day, her dad said, "Anna, I have a special job for you. You can help me shear the sheep. Do you know what that means?"

Anna nodded. She had seen her dad do it before. He used a big machine to cut off the wool from the sheep. The sheep looked funny without their wool, but they felt cooler and lighter. Anna wanted to try it too.

Her dad gave her a small machine and showed her how to hold it. He said, "Be careful, Anna. The machine is sharp and loud. And the sheep might be scared and run away. You have to be gentle and fast. Can you do it?"

Anna said, "Yes, dad. I can do it. I want to make the sheep happy." She followed her dad to the field where the sheep were grazing. Her dad picked a sheep and started to shear it. Anna watched and waited for her turn.

She saw a sheep that looked friendly and fluffy. She walked towards it with her machine. She said, "Hello, sheep. I'm Anna. I'm going to shear you. Don't be afraid. It will be over soon." She turned on the machine and touched the sheep's wool.

But the sheep did not like it. It felt a tickle and a buzz. It jumped and ran away from Anna. Anna chased after it, but the sheep was faster. It ran across the field, past the fence, and into the woods. Anna did not give up. She ran after the sheep, hoping to catch it.

She did not see the sign that said, "Beware of the bees". She did not hear the buzzing sound. She did not notice the hive hanging from the tree. She only saw the sheep. She reached out to grab it, but the sheep dodged her. She bumped into the tree and shook the hive.

The bees came out, angry and stinging. They flew around Anna and the sheep, making them scream and run. Anna dropped her machine and ran back to the field. The sheep followed her, still with its wool. They reached the fence and jumped over it. They ran to Anna's dad, who was waiting for them.

He saw the bees and the wool and the machine. He understood what happened. He said, "Oh, Anna. I'm sorry. You did not succeed in shearing the sheep. But you did succeed in making a spicy adventure. Are you okay?"

Anna nodded. She was okay, but she felt sad and sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, dad. I tried to help you, but I made a mess. The sheep is still fluffy. The machine is broken. The bees are mad. And I have some stings. They hurt."

Her dad hugged her and said, "It's okay, Anna. You don't have to be sorry. You tried your best. And you learned something new. Shearing sheep is not easy. It takes practice and patience. And sometimes, things go wrong. But you are brave and smart. And I'm proud of you."

He took her to the house and gave her some ice and honey. He said, "The ice will make the stings feel better. The honey will make your mouth feel sweet. And tomorrow, we can try again. Maybe with a different sheep. And a different machine. And no bees. What do you say?"

Anna smiled and said, "Okay, dad. I say yes. I want to try again. I want to shear the sheep. And I want to make you happy." She hugged her dad and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you."

Her dad said, "I love you too, Anna. You are my little helper. And my little hero."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing outside when she saw a bright butterfly. She followed the butterfly and it led her to a tree. There was a message tied to the tree that said, "Help! I'm lost!" 

Lily started to panic because she didn't know what to do. She decided to ask her mommy for help. Her mommy read the message and told Lily that they needed to find the person who wrote it. They looked all around the park and finally found a little boy who was crying. 

It turns out that the little boy had wandered away from his mommy and couldn't find her. Lily's mommy called the boy's mommy and they were reunited. The boy was very happy and gave Lily a big hug. From that day on, Lily knew that if she ever saw a message like that again, she should always ask for help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore the desert with his mommy and daddy. One day, they found a big cactus with great thorns. Timmy's daddy urged him to stay away from it, but Timmy wanted to touch it.

Timmy said, "I want to touch the cactus, it looks so great!"

His mommy said, "No, Timmy, it's not safe. The thorns can hurt you."

But Timmy didn't listen and reached out to touch the cactus. Suddenly, he felt a sharp pain in his hand. He had pricked his finger on one of the thorns.

Timmy cried and cried, and his mommy and daddy rushed him to the hospital. The doctor tried to help, but it was too late. Timmy's finger got infected and he had to have it cut off.

The boy was curious and decided to go and look for the person who wrote the note. He ran far away, even though his parents told him not to.

He soon arrived at a deep dark cave. He spotted a figure inside and shouted out; 'I'm here to save you!'

The figure turned out to be an old wolf. The wolf said; 'If you want to save me, you must give me a piece of your wealth'. The boy nodded and said; 'Yes, I will give you something'. 

But the wolf tricked him and kept all the boy's wealth for himself. The boy felt helpless and ran back home.

When he arrived home, all his family members were waiting for him. His parents were angry but also very relieved.

The moral of the story is that we should always be careful and never believe everything we see.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate little bird. The bird was so small that it never had seen the world before. One day, while the little bird was flying, it came across a bowl of rice. The delicate little bird was scared and flew away. The other bird shouted after it, "Just remember, it is important to share and be kind." 

The little bird thought long and hard about what the other bird said. Then the little bird had an idea. The next day, it came back to the bowl of rice and invited all the other birds to enjoy the rice together, instead of being selfish. 

All the birds happily met at the bowl of rice every day. Everyone appreciated that the little, delicate bird was so kind to share with everyone. When the birds shared the rice, they were much happier than when they fought over it. 

The moral of this story is, when we share, everyone is happy!

When it was time to go home, Lily reached into her pocket and found the penny was missing. She was sad and thought she had lost it. But then the boy said, "I saw your penny fall out of your pocket. I picked it up and kept it safe for you." Lily was grateful and happy to have such a kind friend.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the park with her mommy. They saw many trees with pretty leaves. Lily wanted to pick a leaf, but her mommy said no.

Suddenly, they saw a fairy. The fairy was very small and had wings. Lily wanted to say hi, but the fairy said, "Kneel down, please." So, Lily and her mommy kneeled down to talk to the fairy.

The fairy said, "I lost my magic wand. Can you help me find it?" Lily and her mommy searched and searched, but they couldn't find the wand. The fairy was sad and flew away.

Lily and her mommy felt bad that they couldn't help the fairy. They went home and talked about how they wished they could have helped her. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny was very thirsty and tired. He walked and walked until he found an oasis. An oasis is a place with water and trees. Benny drank some water and felt strong again.

As Benny rested, he noticed some footprints on the ground. He asked his friend, a wise old owl, "Who made these marks?" The owl replied, "It's the lion. He's very strong and dangerous. You should be careful."

Benny was scared and wanted to leave, but he was still very thirsty. He decided to fill his belly with water before leaving. Suddenly, he heard a loud roar. It was the lion! Benny ran as fast as he could, but the lion was too strong. Benny thought he was done for. But then, the wise old owl swooped in and scared the lion away with his strong wings. Benny was safe and grateful to have such a strong friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, it started to rain very hard. Lily didn't have a shelter to protect herself from the rain, so she got very wet. 

As she walked home, she observed the animals and plants around her. She saw how the birds found shelter in the trees and how the flowers bent down to avoid getting too wet. 

When she got home, her mom gave her a warm bath and some hot chocolate. Lily told her mom about what she had observed outside. Her mom explained to her that even though it was just an ordinary rain, it was important to always be prepared and have a shelter to protect ourselves. 

From that day on, Lily made sure to always have a shelter nearby when she went outside, just like the birds and the flowers. She learned that it's important to observe the world around us and learn from it.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet was very lonely because he had no friends. One day, a big storm came and Tweet got scared. He saw a branch that he thought was strong and safe, so he flew to it. But when he got there, he saw that there was already a bird sitting on it. Tweet didn't know what to do, but he decided to pull the branch down so that the other bird would fall off. 

But then, Tweet realized that what he was doing was not nice. He felt bad for trying to hurt the other bird. So, instead of pulling the branch down, he asked the other bird if they could share the branch together. The other bird agreed and they both sat on the branch and waited out the storm. 

After the storm had passed, the other bird thanked Tweet for being kind and not pulling the branch down. Tweet learned that being mean to others is not the right thing to do and that sharing and being kind is much better. From that day on, Tweet had a new friend and was no longer lonely.

"I want some berries," said the squirrel. "I saw you feeding the bird earlier. Do you have any more?"

Lily remembered the berries she had found in the forest and gave them to the squirrel. The squirrel was very grateful and ran away happily. From that day on, Lily always carried extra berries with her when she went to play in the forest.

"Can I play with the queen?" Ben asked Anna.

"No, she is mine. You can play with the other dolls," Anna said.

"But I like the queen. She is pretty and smart. Please, let me have a turn," Ben said.

"No, no, no. The queen is mine. Go away," Anna said. She was very selfish.

Ben felt sad and angry. He did not like how Anna treated him. He decided to play with something else. He saw a big ball on the other side of the garden. He ran to get it. He threw the ball high in the air and caught it. He had fun with the ball.

Anna saw Ben playing with the ball. She wanted the ball too. She left the queen doll on the grass and ran to Ben.

"Can I play with the ball?" Anna asked Ben.

"No, it is mine. You can play with the queen," Ben said.

"But I like the ball. It is round and bouncy. Please, let me have a turn," Anna said.

"No, no, no. The ball is mine. Go away," Ben said. He was not selfish. He was just teaching Anna a lesson.

Anna felt sad and angry. She did not like how Ben treated her. She decided to go back to the queen doll. But when she got there, she saw a big dog. The dog had found the queen doll on the grass. The dog liked the queen doll too. He picked it up with his mouth and ran away.

"Hey, come back! That is my queen!" Anna shouted. She chased the dog, but the dog was faster. He ran out of the garden with the queen doll.

Anna cried. She had lost the queen doll. She wished she had shared it with Ben. She learned that being selfish was not good. She said sorry to Ben and asked him to play with the ball. Ben forgave her and shared the ball. They played together and had fun. They were happy.

Tom and Lily were playing with their ball in the park. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball went too far and they had to look for it in the grass or behind a tree.

One time, the ball went over the fence and into the road. Tom and Lily ran to the fence and saw a big car coming. The car hit the ball and made a loud noise. The ball popped and flew in the air. Tom and Lily were scared and sad.

A man got out of the car and looked at the ball. He was angry and said, "Who threw this ball in the road? You are very careless! You could have caused an accident!"

Tom and Lily did not know what to say. They felt sorry for the man and the ball. They did not mean to throw the ball in the road. They wanted to explain, but they did not know how.

A woman came from the park and saw what happened. She was Tom and Lily's mom. She went to the fence and said, "I'm sorry, sir. These are my children. They were playing with their ball and it went over the fence by mistake. They did not see your car. They are not careless, they are just little. Please don't be mad at them."

The man looked at the woman and the children. He saw that they were honest and sorry. He felt less angry and more calm. He said, "I'm sorry, too. I was too harsh. I know you did not do it on purpose. I'm glad no one was hurt. Here, take this money and buy a new ball."

The woman thanked the man and took the money. She hugged Tom and Lily and said, "Let's go home, kids. We'll get a new ball tomorrow. And remember, always be careful when you play near the road. The road is not a safe place for balls or children."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We understand. Thank you, sir. We're sorry for the trouble."

"Hey, you kids, stop throwing snowballs at my chimney!" he shouted. "You almost hit me! I was cleaning the chimney for Santa. He won't come if it's not clean and sweet!"

Lily and Tom were scared. They did not mean to hurt the man. They thought he was Santa. They ran away from the house and back to their snowman.

"Sorry, mister, sorry!" they said. "We did not know you were there. We thought you were Santa. We just wanted to say hello!"

The man heard them and felt sorry. He was not really angry. He was just surprised and sore. He waved at them and smiled.

"It's okay, kids, it's okay!" he said. "I'm not Santa, but I work for him. I'm a chimney sweeper. I make the chimneys clean and sweet for Santa. He likes to slide down them and leave presents for good children like you. But don't throw snowballs at them, please. They might break or block them. Then Santa won't be able to come!"

Lily and Tom nodded. They understood. They said sorry again and thanked the man for his work. They wished him a merry Christmas and went home with their snowman. They hoped Santa would come and find their chimney clean and sweet. They hoped he would leave them some nice toys and candy. They were good children and they loved Santa.

Sara was very happy. It was her birthday and she had a big cake and many gifts. She wanted to open them all, but her mom said she had to wait for her dad to come home. He was at work and he would be back soon.

Sara waited and waited, but her dad did not come. She looked at the clock and saw it was very late. She felt sad and angry. Why did her dad forget her birthday? She did not want to wait anymore. She decided to open one gift, just one. She picked the one with the shiny wrap and the big bow. She tore the wrap and saw a book. She liked books, but she wanted something else. She opened another gift, and another, and another. She did not like any of them. She threw them on the floor and cried.

Her mom heard her cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and the tears and felt sorry for Sara. She hugged her and said, "I know you are upset, but you should not open your gifts without your dad. He did not forget your birthday. He has a surprise for you. He will be here any minute. Please, be patient and kind."

Sara did not listen. She pushed her mom away and said, "I don't care. I don't want his surprise. I don't want him. He is always late. He is always busy. He is always harsh. He does not love me."

Her mom was shocked and hurt. She did not know what to say. She left Sara alone and went to the kitchen. She hoped her dad would come soon and make things better.

Sara stayed in her room and cried. She did not want to see anyone. She did not want to celebrate. She did not want to be happy. She wished she could forget her birthday.

Then, she heard a knock on the door. She did not answer. She heard her dad's voice. He said, "Sara, can I come in? I have something for you. I'm sorry I'm late. I had a problem at work, but I fixed it. I love you very much. Please, open the door."

Sara did not move. She did not want to talk to him. She did not want to see him. She did not want to love him.

He knocked again. He said, "Sara, please, don't be mad at me. I know you are disappointed, but I have a good reason. I have a big surprise for you. It's something you always wanted. It's something very special. It's something I made for you. Please, let me show you."

Sara was curious. She wondered what he had for her. She wondered what he made for her. She wondered if he really loved her. She decided to give him a chance. She wiped her tears and opened the door.

She saw her dad holding a big box with a red wrap and a gold bow. He smiled and said, "Happy birthday, Sara. This is for you. I hope you like it. I made it with all my love."

Sara took the box and opened it. She gasped and smiled. She could not believe her eyes. Inside the box, there was a dollhouse. A beautiful dollhouse, with many rooms and furniture and dolls. A dollhouse that looked like her own house, but smaller and prettier. A dollhouse that was her dream.

She hugged her dad and said, "Thank you, dad. I love it. I love you. I'm sorry I was mean to you. I'm sorry I opened the other gifts. I'm sorry I said you forgot me."

He hugged her back and said, "It's okay, Sara. I understand. I'm sorry I was late. I'm sorry I was busy. I'm sorry I was harsh. I did not forget you. I never will. You are my best gift. You are my princess."

They kissed and laughed and went to the living room. They joined her mom and ate the cake and played with the dollhouse. They had a wonderful time. They were a happy family. Sara did not forget her birthday. She remembered it as the best day ever.

She ran after the bubble, trying to reach it with her hand. Tom followed her, laughing. The bubble moved with the wind, and Sara had to stretch her arm to touch it. But when she did, the bubble popped and wet her hand.

"Aw, it's gone!" Sara said, feeling sad.

"Don't worry, Sara, there are more bubbles!" Tom said, blowing more air through the wand. "See, this one is shiny and colorful!"

He held the wand in front of Sara, and she saw a bubble that had many colors on its surface. It looked like a rainbow. She smiled and clapped her hands.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Sara said. "Can I try?"

Tom nodded and gave her the wand. Sara dipped it in the soap and blew air through the hole. She made a bubble that was also shiny and colorful. She was happy and proud.

"Look, Tom, I made a bubble like yours!" Sara said, showing him her bubble.

But then, something mysterious happened. The bubble did not float in the air like the others. It stayed on the wand, and it did not pop. It looked like a ball of glass.

"What is that?" Tom asked, surprised.

"I don't know," Sara said, curious. "Maybe it's a magic bubble!"

They both stared at the bubble, wondering what it was and what it could do. They did not notice that a man in a black coat and a hat was watching them from behind a tree. He had a big bag and a net. He wanted to catch the magic bubble and take it away. He waited for the right moment to sneak up on them and grab the wand. But he did not know that the magic bubble had a secret. It was not just a bubble. It was a friend.

Tara and Tim were twins who loved to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big otter. The otter was soft and brown and had a long tail. Tara and Tim liked to pretend that the otter was their friend and they took turns to hug it and talk to it.

One day, they decided to have a race with the otter. They put the otter on the floor and each held one end of its tail. They said, "Ready, set, go!" and pulled the otter towards them. The otter slid on the floor and made a funny noise. Tara and Tim laughed and pulled harder.

But then, something happened. The otter's tail came off! Tara and Tim looked at each other and gasped. They had broken their favorite toy! They felt sad and sorry. They did not know what to do.

They ran to their mom and showed her the otter and the tail. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We broke the otter. We wanted to win the race, but we pulled too hard. Can you fix it?"

Mom looked at the otter and the tail and smiled. She said, "Don't worry, my loves. I can fix it. You did not mean to break it. You were just having fun. But next time, be gentle with your toys. They are not for racing. They are for cuddling and playing."

She took the otter and the tail and went to her sewing box. She took a needle and a thread and sewed the tail back to the otter. She made a small knot and cut the thread. She gave the otter back to Tara and Tim and said, "Here you go. Your otter is as good as new. And look, he has a special mark on his tail. He is the most original otter in the world. He is lucky to have you as his friends."

Tara and Tim hugged their mom and thanked her. They hugged their otter and said, "We are sorry, otter. We love you. You are the best otter in the world. You are our friend."

They took the otter to their room and played with it gently. They did not race with it anymore. They shared it and talked to it and made it happy. They learned to be kind to their toys and to each other. They did not care who would win. They cared about having fun.

Tommy liked to play soldier with his big brother Jake. Jake had a green hat and a toy gun that made loud noises. Tommy wanted to be like Jake, but he was too small to wear the hat or hold the gun. Jake said Tommy could be his helper and gave him a red scarf to wear around his neck.

One day, Jake and Tommy were playing soldier in the backyard. They pretended to hide behind the bushes and shoot at the bad guys. Jake said, "Tommy, you stay here and watch for enemies. I'll go and check the fence." Tommy nodded and tried to look brave. He wrapped the scarf around his face and held a stick like a gun.

But Tommy was bored and curious. He wanted to see what Jake was doing. He left his spot and followed Jake to the fence. He saw Jake climb over the fence and disappear into the woods. Tommy wanted to go too, but he was scared of the dark trees. He decided to wait for Jake to come back.

He waited and waited, but Jake did not come back. Tommy started to feel cold and hungry. He wondered if Jake was lost or hurt. He wished he had stayed with Jake. He wished he had not worn the scarf, because it made him hot and itchy. He tried to take it off, but it was stuck. He pulled and pulled, but it only got tighter. He started to cry.

Then he heard a voice. "Hey, kid, are you okay?" It was a real soldier, wearing a green uniform and a helmet. He had a big gun and a walkie-talkie. He had seen Tommy from the road and came to help. He gently untied the scarf from Tommy's neck and asked him his name and where he lived. Tommy told him everything. The soldier said, "Don't worry, I'll find your brother and take you home. You're a brave kid, you know that? You're wearing the perfect scarf for a soldier. It's red, like courage and love." Tommy smiled and felt better. He liked the soldier. He hoped Jake would like him too.

As they drove away, Timmy asked his dad why the man was bald. His dad explained that some people lose their hair when they get older. Timmy thought about this and wondered if he would ever be bald. But then he remembered the apples he loved to taste and decided that he would rather keep his hair and keep eating apples.

"Of course," said her mom. "We can fold up as many candles as you want."

From then on, Lily and her mom folded up all of their candles when they were almost gone. It became their special bedtime routine. And every night, Lily would light a new candle and watch it flicker before blowing it out and folding it up for later.

They break the rock into smaller pieces and put some in each engine. They turn on the switches and watch their trains go.

"Yes, they are!" Kim says. "But we have to be careful. We don't want them to crash."

"Dan, you have to yield!" Kim says. "Your train is on my track!"

"No, you have to yield!" Dan says. "My train is bigger and stronger!"

They both hold on to their switches and don't let go. They hope that their trains will stop or turn by themselves.

But their trains don't stop or turn. They keep going faster and faster. They hit each other with a loud bang. The engines break and the coal flies out. The trains stop and smoke.

Dan and Kim are shocked and scared. They run to their trains and see the damage.

"Oh no, look what we did!" Dan says. "We broke our trains and wasted our coal!"

"I'm sorry, Dan," Kim says. "We should have yielded and shared the track."

"I'm sorry, too, Kim," Dan says. "We should have listened to each other and been more careful."

Lily's mom came into the room and saw what she had made. "What a beautiful shape!" she exclaimed. Lily smiled and felt proud of herself. But then, her mom noticed something strange. "Why did you shrug your shoulders?" she asked.

Lily didn't know what to say. She had shrunk her shoulders because she knew deep down that her creation wasn't perfect. Later that day, Lily's mom showed her how to add little details to her clay creation to make it even better. From then on, Lily never shrugged her shoulders again when she was creating something new.

Ben and Lily liked to play near the old mill. It was a big house with a wheel that turned in the water. Sometimes they saw birds and fish and frogs there. They also liked to look for shiny things in the dirt.

One day, they found a small box with a lock. It was rusty and dirty, but they thought it might have something good inside. They tried to open it, but it was too hard.

"Maybe we need a key," Ben said.

"Or maybe we can break it," Lily said.

They looked for a rock or a stick, but they could not find anything. They were about to give up, when they heard a voice.

"Hello, children. What are you doing here?"

They turned around and saw an old man with a long beard and a hat. He was holding a cane and a bag. He smiled at them.

"We found this box, sir. But we can't open it," Ben said.

"Let me see," the old man said. He took the box and looked at it. He nodded and said, "This is a very special box. It belongs to me. I left it here a long time ago, when I worked at the mill. It has a gift inside, for someone who is gifted."

"Who is gifted, sir?" Lily asked.

"Someone who can do something very well, or has a special talent," the old man said. He looked at Ben and Lily and said, "Do you have any gifts, children?"

Ben and Lily thought for a moment. Ben liked to draw and paint. He could make beautiful pictures of the mill and the animals. Lily liked to sing and dance. She could make lovely sounds and move gracefully.

"I can draw and paint, sir," Ben said.

"I can sing and dance, sir," Lily said.

The old man smiled and said, "Then you are both gifted, children. And I have a gift for you. Here, take this key. It will open the box. But you have to promise me something. You have to share the gift with each other, and with anyone who needs it. Can you do that?"

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, sir. We promise."

The old man gave them the key and said, "Good. Now, open the box and see what's inside."

Ben and Lily used the key and opened the box. They gasped and smiled. Inside the box, there were many things. There were crayons and paints and brushes and paper for Ben. There were ribbons and bells and feathers and flowers for Lily. There were also candies and cookies and chocolates for both of them.

"Wow! This is amazing!" Ben said.

"Thank you, sir! Thank you so much!" Lily said.

They looked at the old man, but he was gone. They only saw his hat and his cane and his bag. They were lying on the ground, near the mill. They picked them up and wiped them with their hands. They saw a note on the bag. It said:

"Dear children, I hope you enjoy your gifts. They are from the mill fairy. He likes to help gifted children like you. He also likes to play tricks. He turned me into an old man, so I could give you the box. But now he has turned me back into a bird. I have to fly away, but I will always remember you. Be kind, be happy, be gifted. Love, the mill fairy."

Ben and Lily looked at the sky and saw a bird flying away. It was blue and yellow and red. It sang a beautiful song. They waved and said, "Goodbye, mill fairy! Thank you for the gifts!"

They hugged each other and laughed. They decided to use their gifts and make something for the mill fairy. They also decided to share their gifts with their friends and family. They were very happy. They knew they had met a very special friend. They knew they had a very special day.

Timmy tried to resist the cake, but he couldn't help himself. He opened the container and took a big bite. It was so tasty! But then he remembered his promise to his mommy. He felt sad and guilty. He knew he shouldn't have eaten the cake.

Timmy learned that promises are important and he should always keep them. He also learned that it's okay to have treats once in a while, but he should always eat healthy food first. From that day on, Timmy kept his promises and ate healthy food. And when he did have a treat, he enjoyed it even more because he knew he deserved it.

"OK," Lily said. "But we have to ask Mom first."

They ran to Mom and asked her if they could go to the park. Mom said yes, but they had to be careful and come back soon. She gave them a snack and a bottle of water.

Tom and Lily walked to the park. They saw some birds, some flowers, and some dogs. But they were not very excited. They had seen them before.

Then they heard a loud noise. It sounded like a trumpet. They looked around and saw a big gray animal. It had a long nose, big ears, and a tail. It was an elephant!

"Wow!" Tom said. "Look, Lily, an elephant!"

"Wow!" Lily said. "Where did it come from?"

They ran to the elephant. It was friendly. It lifted its nose and touched their heads. It made the trumpet noise again. Tom and Lily laughed.

"Hello, elephant," Tom said. "What is your name?"

The elephant made another noise. It sounded like "Ella".

"Ella," Lily repeated. "That's a nice name. Do you want to play with us?"

Ella nodded. She picked up a ball with her nose and threw it to Tom. Tom caught it and threw it back. Lily joined the game. They had a lot of fun.

They forgot about the time. They forgot about their snack and water. They only wanted to play with Ella.

But then they heard Mom's voice. She was calling them.

"Tom! Lily! Come back! It's time to go home!"

Tom and Lily looked at Mom. They looked at Ella. They felt sad.

"Bye, Ella," Tom said. "Thank you for playing with us. You are not dull. You are fun."

"Bye, Ella," Lily said. "We will miss you. You are our friend."

Ella made a sad noise. She touched their heads again. She waved her nose. She said goodbye.

Tom and Lily ran to Mom. They hugged her. They told her about Ella. Mom smiled. She was happy they had fun. But she was also surprised. She had never seen an elephant in the park before.

They walked home. They looked back at the park. They hoped to see Ella again. They wondered where she came from. They wondered where she would go. They wondered if she would remember them. They wondered if they would ever play with her again.

They ran to the movie theater and gave their tickets to the man. The man looked at them and smiled. He said they were brave and smart. He said he would let them in, but he warned them that the movie was very scary. He said they could leave anytime if they felt scared.

Lily and Sam thanked the man and went inside. They found seats and waited for the movie to start. They were excited and curious. They wanted to see the lion, the bear and the snake.

The movie started and the lights went off. Lily and Sam watched the movie. They saw the lion, the bear and the snake. They also saw many other things. They saw fire, blood, guns and screams. They saw people and animals get hurt and die. They saw scary faces and scary sounds.

Lily and Sam felt scared. They felt very scared. They wanted to leave, but they did not want to waste their money. They did not want to look like cowards. They tried to be brave and stay.

But the movie got scarier and scarier. Lily and Sam could not take it anymore. They started to cry and shake. They grabbed each other and ran out of the theater. They did not care about their money or their pride. They only cared about being safe and happy.

They ran to their moms and hugged them. They told them what happened. Their moms were angry and worried. They said they should have listened to them. They said the movie was not for them. They said they were too young and too sensitive.

Lily and Sam felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry and they learned their lesson. They said they would not do it again. They said they would only watch movies that were good and fun for them.

Their moms forgave them and hugged them. They said they loved them and they were glad they were okay. They said they were still brave and smart, but they also needed to be careful and wise. They said they would help them find better movies to watch.

Lily and Sam felt better and smiled. They thanked their moms and said they loved them too. They said they would be more careful and wise next time. They said they still liked to play together, but they did not like to watch scary movies.

The moral of the story is: Be careful what you wish for. Not everything that looks brave and fun is good for you. Listen to your parents and trust your feelings. Choose movies that are suitable and enjoyable for you.

She liked things that were smooth and soft, like her blanket and her doll. She did not like things that were rough and hard, like the wall and the table.

One day, she saw a new thing in the kitchen. It was a cupboard that her mom had brought home from the store. It was big and brown and had a shiny handle. Lily wondered what was inside. She decided to poke it and find out.

She walked over to the cupboard and reached for the handle. She pulled it and the door opened. She saw many things inside. There were boxes and cans and jars and bags. Some had pictures of food on them, some had words that she could not read. She poked one of the boxes and it made a crinkly sound. She liked that sound. Lily turned around and saw her mom standing in the doorway. She had a big spoon in her hand and a bowl on the counter. She was making something for lunch.

Her mom sighed and walked over to her. She picked up the jar and put it back in the cupboard. She closed the door and locked it with a key. She said, "Lily, you can't poke everything you see. They flew together every day. Tom and Tim were very happy. The calm pilot and his little bird friend loved to fly in the sky. And every day, Tim would repeat, "I can fly like you!"

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They had to cross a busy road with a lot of traffic. Tim's mom said, "Tim, hold my hand and we will cross the road together." Tim held his mom's hand and they crossed the road.

At the park, Tim saw a big slide. He wanted to slide down it. His mom said, "Be careful, Tim. Make sure to sit on the seat and hold on tight." Tim sat on the seat and slid down the slide. He felt fine and had a lot of fun.

After playing for a while, Tim and his mom went back to the road to cross it again. But this time, Tim did not hold his mom's hand. He ran into the traffic and got hit by a car. His mom cried and said, "I told you to hold my hand, Tim." Tim was hurt and sad. The day did not end well for Tim.

The doctor put the band-aid on Tim's leg. Tim felt better and said, "Thank you, doctor!" They went home, and Tim promised to be more careful when he played. From that day on, Tim was still restless, but he always remembered to be safe.
