One day, in the summer, they decided to play with the truck in the backyard. They made a road with some rocks and sticks, and pretended to go on a long trip. Lily drove the truck first, and Ben sat next to her. They made vroom-vroom sounds and laughed.

"Can I drive now?" Ben asked after a while.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said. She gave him the truck and moved to the other seat.

Ben was very happy. He wanted to show Lily how fast he could drive. He pushed the truck forward and backward, making it go faster and faster. He did not see the big rock that was in the road.

"Ben, watch out!" Lily shouted.

But it was too late. Ben hit the rock with the truck, and the truck flew in the air. It landed on the grass with a loud crash. The truck was broken. The wheels came off, and the noise maker stopped working.

Lily and Ben were very sad. They loved their truck, and now it was ruined. They did not know what to do.

They heard their mom calling them from the house. "Lily, Ben, come inside. I have a surprise for you."

They ran to the house, hoping the surprise would make them feel better. They followed their mom to the living room, where they saw a big box with a bow on it.

"What is it, mom?" Lily asked.

"Open it and see," mom said.

They opened the box, and their eyes widened. Inside was a new toy car. It was bigger and shinier than their old truck. It had lights and horns and a remote control. It could go forward and reverse, and turn left and right.

"Wow, mom, thank you!" Lily and Ben said.

I bought this car a few weeks ago, and I was saving it for your birthday. But I thought you might like it now, since it's summer and you have more time to play."

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt a little guilty. They had not told their mom about their broken truck. They wondered if she knew.

They decided to tell her the truth. They told her how they had crashed their truck, and how sorry they were. They said they would be more careful with their new car.

Mom hugged them and said, "It's OK, my loves. I know accidents happen. I'm glad you told me the truth. I'm proud of you for being honest and responsible. And don't worry about the truck. I can fix it. Maybe we can do it together, as a fun project."

Lily and Ben smiled. They felt better. They loved their mom, and they loved their new car. They also loved their old truck, and they hoped it would be OK soon. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful, to share, and to tell the truth. They also learned that mom was always there for them, and that she had a persistent way of making them happy.

"I want to add carrots and peas," Lily said.

"No, I want to add corn and beans," Tom said.

They both reached for the same toy spoon and pulled it hard. The spoon broke in half and the toy pot fell off the stove. The soup spilled on the floor and made a big mess.

"Look what you did!" Lily shouted.

"It's your fault!" Tom shouted back.

They started to cry and yell at each other. Their mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the broken spoon, the spilled soup, and the angry twins.

"What's going on here?" she asked.

"Lily and Tom were quarreling over the soup," the stove said.

The stove was not a real stove, but a harmless toy that could talk. It liked to tell stories and jokes, but sometimes it also told the truth.

Mom looked at the stove and smiled. She knew it was a harmless toy, but she also knew it could help her teach the twins a lesson.

"Thank you, stove, for telling me what happened," she said. "Lily and Tom, do you know that quarreling is not nice? It can hurt your feelings and break your things. You should share and take turns, and say sorry when you make a mistake."

Lily and Tom felt sorry for quarreling and breaking the spoon. They hugged each other and said sorry.

"We're sorry, mom," they said.

"We're sorry, stove," they said.

The stove was happy to see them make up. It said, "That's okay, Lily and Tom. I'm glad you're friends again. Do you want to hear a funny story about a soup that made everyone laugh?"

Lily and Tom nodded and smiled. They cleaned up the mess and listened to the stove's story. They learned to play nicely and not to quarrel.

Sara was a wealthy girl who had many toys and clothes. She liked to keep everything for herself and did not share with anyone. One day, she saw a cute kitten on the street. She wanted to keep the kitten too, so she took it home and hid it in her room.

The kitten was scared and hungry. It meowed and scratched the door, but Sara did not care. She only wanted to play with it when she felt like it. She did not give it any food or water or love.

Her mother heard the kitten's cries and went to Sara's room. She opened the door and saw the poor kitten. She was angry and sad. She said to Sara, "How could you be so selfish and cruel? This kitten is a living thing, not a toy. It needs care and kindness, not neglect and abuse. You cannot keep the kitten. You have to give it back to the street or find a good home for it."

Sara did not want to give up the kitten. She cried and screamed and said, "No, it is mine! I found it, I keep it! Go away, leave me alone!" She grabbed the kitten and ran away from her mother.

She ran outside and crossed the street, without looking for cars. A big truck was coming fast and did not see her. It hit her and the kitten. They both died.

The moral of the story is: Greed and selfishness can lead to tragedy. We should be generous and compassionate to others, especially to animals. We should not keep what we do not need or deserve.

One day, they decide to have a contest. Who can build the highest tower with their blocks? They split the blocks into two piles, one for Tom and one for Anna. They start to build their towers on opposite sides of the room. They stack the blocks carefully, trying not to make them fall.

"Look at my tower, Anna!" Tom says. "It is very high and strong. I will win the contest!"

"No, Tom, look at my tower!" Anna says. "It is higher and prettier. I will win the contest!"

They keep building their towers, adding more and more blocks. They are both very proud of their towers. They want to have the victory.

But then, something happens. A loud noise comes from outside. It is a big truck. It makes the floor shake. The blocks start to wobble. Tom and Anna watch in horror as their towers collapse. The blocks fall to the ground, making a mess.

"Oh no!" Tom and Anna cry. "Our towers are gone!"

They look at each other, sad and angry. They both think it is not fair. They both want to blame the other one. They start to argue.

"It is your fault, Anna! Your tower was too close to mine. It made mine fall!"

"No, it is your fault, Tom! Your tower was too big and heavy. It made mine fall!"

They shout and point at each other. They do not listen to each other. They do not want to share their blocks anymore.

But then, they hear another noise. It is their mom. She comes into the room. She sees the blocks on the floor and the children fighting. She is not happy.

"What is going on here?" she asks. "Why are you making so much noise? Why are you not playing nicely?"

Tom and Anna stop arguing. They look at their mom. They know they are in trouble. They try to explain.

"We were having a contest, mom. We wanted to see who could build the highest tower. But then the truck came and made our towers fall. And then we started to fight. We are sorry, mom."

Their mom sighs. She looks at the blocks and the children. She has an idea.

"I see. Well, I am glad you are sorry. But you know, fighting is not a good way to solve a problem. And having a contest is not the only way to have fun. Why don't you try something else? Why don't you work together and build something with your blocks? Something that you both like. Something that you can share. Maybe then you will have more fun and less trouble."

Tom and Anna think about their mom's idea. They look at each other. They feel a little ashamed. They realize they were not very nice to each other. They remember they are friends. They nod.

"Okay, mom. We will try that. We will work together and build something. Thank you, mom."

Their mom smiles. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She leaves them to play.

Tom and Anna pick up their blocks. They start to talk. They ask each other what they like. They agree on a plan. They start to build. They help each other. They compliment each other. They laugh and smile.

They build a big castle with their blocks. It has walls, towers, doors, windows and flags. It is clear and colorful. It is beautiful and strong. It is their castle. They are happy.

They look at their castle. They look at each other. They give each other a high five. They have a victory. A victory of friendship.

"Can we read more words, mom?" Lily asked.

One day, a little squirrel named Sam found a big nut in the forest. He was very happy, because he liked nuts a lot. He wanted to take the nut to his home in the tree, but it was too heavy for him. He tried to push it, pull it, and roll it, but it did not move.

"Help, help!" he cried. "Who can help me with this nut?"

A big owl heard him and flew down from a branch. He looked at the nut and said, "This is not a nut, this is an ancient egg. It is very old and very rare. It belongs to the museum, not to you."

Sam did not know what a museum was, but he did not want to give up his nut. He said, "No, this is my nut. I found it first. It is mine."

The owl shook his head and said, "You are wrong, little squirrel. This egg is not for eating, it is for hatching. Inside, there is a baby dragon. He will come out soon and he will glow in the dark. He will be very beautiful and very powerful. You cannot keep him as a pet, he will be too big and too wild."

Sam did not believe the owl. He thought he was lying to take his nut away. He said, "You are silly, big owl. There is no such thing as a dragon. There is only a nut. And it is my nut."

The owl sighed and said, "You will see, little squirrel. You will see." He flew away and left Sam alone with the nut.

Sam was happy again. He hugged his nut and said, "You are my nut. You are the best nut ever. I will never let you go."

But then, he heard a crack. And then, another crack. And then, a loud roar. He looked at his nut and saw a hole. And from the hole, a head came out. A head with scales, horns, and teeth. A head that glowed in the dark. A head that belonged to a baby dragon.

Sam was scared. He dropped his nut and ran away. He ran as fast as he could, until he reached his home in the tree. He hid under his blanket and said, "That was not a nut. That was a dragon. And he was not mine. He was scary."

The owl was right. He always was.

"Sure, but you have to be careful. Don't let go of the balloon until the man says so. He is the wise man who knows when is the best time to release the balloons," her mom said.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the soil and look for bugs and worms. Sometimes they found shiny stones or old coins. They put them in a jar and pretended they were treasure.

One day, they saw something very strange in the soil. It was round and black and had a hole in it. It looked like a big eye. Lily and Tom were curious and scared. They wondered what it was.

"Maybe it is a monster's eye," Lily said.

"Maybe it is a magic eye," Tom said.

They decided to poke it with a stick. When they did, they heard a loud beep. The eye opened and a voice came out.

"Hello, hello, who are you?" the voice said.

Lily and Tom jumped back. They were very surprised. The eye was not an eye, but a machine. A mysterious machine that could talk.

"Who are you?" Lily asked.

"I am a robot. I was buried here a long time ago. I was waiting for someone to find me. You are the first ones to talk to me," the machine said.

"A robot? What is a robot?" Tom asked.

"A robot is a machine that can do things. I can move, talk, learn, and play. Do you want to play with me?" the machine asked.

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They were still scared, but also curious. They wanted to know more about the robot and what it could do.

"Okay, we will play with you. But you have to be nice and not hurt us," Lily said.

"Of course, I will be nice and not hurt you. I am your friend. What is your name?" the machine asked.

"I am Lily and this is Tom. What is your name?" Lily replied.

"I do not have a name. You can give me one," the machine said.

Lily and Tom thought for a moment. They wanted to give the machine a good name. A name that suited it.

"How about Beep? Because you beep when you talk," Tom suggested.

"Beep. I like that name. Thank you, Tom. Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. Now, let us play," the machine said.

Lily and Tom smiled. They had found a new friend. A mysterious and wonderful friend. They played with Beep all afternoon. They taught him how to dig, how to count, how to sing, and how to have fun. Beep was very happy. He had found his first friends. He hoped they would come back and play with him again.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They lived on a farm with many animals. They liked to play with the cows, the pigs, the chickens and the sheep. They also liked to whisper secrets to each other.

One day, they saw a new animal on the farm. It was big and brown and had horns. It made a loud noise like "moo". Lily and Tom were curious. They wanted to know what it was.

They ran to the farmer and asked him. "What is that animal, farmer?" they said.

The farmer smiled and said, "That is a bull. He is a male cow. He is here to make more cows."

Lily and Tom nodded. They thought the bull was interesting. They wanted to see him closer.

They went to the fence and looked at the bull. He was eating grass. He looked at them with his big eyes. He seemed friendly.

Lily and Tom whispered to each other. "Do you think he likes us?" Lily said.

"Maybe. Let's say hello to him." Tom said.

They leaned over the fence and said, "Hello, bull. We are Lily and Tom. We live on this farm. We are your friends."

The bull heard them and raised his head. He snorted and shook his horns. He did not like them. He did not want them near him. He was angry.

He charged at the fence and hit it with his horns. The fence broke and the bull ran out. He chased Lily and Tom across the field. He wanted to hurt them.

Lily and Tom were scared. They screamed and ran. They did not know what to do.

The farmer heard them and saw the bull. He was worried. He ran after them with a rope. He wanted to catch the bull and put him back.

He shouted at Lily and Tom. "Run to the barn! Run to the barn! The bull is dangerous!"

Lily and Tom heard him and ran to the barn. They opened the door and went inside. They closed the door behind them. They were safe.

The farmer caught the bull and tied him to a tree. He was angry too. He went to the barn and opened the door. He saw Lily and Tom hiding behind a haystack. He was relieved.

He said to them, "Are you okay? Are you hurt?"

Lily and Tom shook their heads. They were not hurt. They were sorry.

They said to the farmer, "We are sorry, farmer. We did not know the bull was dangerous. We wanted to be his friends. We were ignorant."

The farmer sighed and said, "It's okay. You did not know. But you should never go near the bull again. He is not friendly. He is wild. He does not like people. You should only play with the animals that are tame and gentle. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They understood. They learned their lesson. They thanked the farmer and hugged him. They said, "We are sorry, farmer. We love you. We love the farm. We love the animals. But not the bull."

The farmer smiled and said, "I love you too. I love the farm. I love the animals. But not the bull. He is going away soon. He is not staying here. Come on, let's go and have some cookies and milk. You must be hungry and thirsty."

Lily and Tom smiled and said, "Yes, please. We are hungry and thirsty. We like cookies and milk. They are yummy."

They followed the farmer to the house. They left the bull behind. They did not look at him again. They did not whisper to him again. They did not want to be his friends. They were not ignorant anymore.

There was a princess who lived in a distant castle. She was very lonely and sad. She had no friends to play with or talk to. She only had her old nanny, who was always busy and strict.

One day, the princess saw a bird outside her window. It was red and yellow and very pretty. The princess opened the window and called to the bird. "Hello, bird. Do you want to be my friend?"

The bird flew to the window and nodded. "Yes, princess. I want to be your friend. You are very kind and sweet."

The princess smiled and asked the bird. "What is your name, bird?"

The bird said. "My name is Sunny. I like to fly and sing and eat worms."

The princess made a face. "Worms? You eat worms? That is yucky."

The bird laughed. "No, princess. Worms are yummy. They are good for me. They make me strong and happy."

The princess was curious. "Can I try a worm, Sunny?"

The bird shook his head. "No, princess. Worms are not good for you. They are bad for you. They make you sick and unhappy."

The princess said. "Oh, I see. Then what do you think I should eat, Sunny?"

The bird said. "You should eat fruits and vegetables and bread and cheese. They are good for you. They make you healthy and cheerful."

The princess nodded. "You are right, Sunny. I like fruits and vegetables and bread and cheese. They are tasty. Do you want to share some with me?"

The bird said. "Yes, princess. I would love to share some with you. You are very generous and friendly."

The princess and the bird ate some food together. They talked and laughed and sang. They became the best of friends. The princess was no longer lonely and sad. She was happy and grateful. She had found a friend in a distant castle.

Sam and Mia went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things on the beach, like shells, crabs, and birds.

One day, they saw something new on the sand. It was big and soft and had long things hanging from it. It was pink and purple and shiny.

"What is that?" Sam asked.

Mia looked at it and said, "I know! It is a jellyfish!"

"A jellyfish?" Sam said. "What is a jellyfish?"

Mia said, "A jellyfish is a thing that lives in the water. It can sting you if you touch it. It hurts a lot."

Sam was curious and wanted to touch it. He reached out his hand.

"Sam, no!" Mia shouted. "Don't touch it!"

But it was too late. Sam touched the jellyfish and felt a sharp pain in his hand. He cried out loud.

"Ow, ow, ow! It stings, it stings!"

Mom and Dad heard Sam's cry and ran to him. They saw the jellyfish on the sand and Sam's hand was red and swollen.

"Oh, Sam, you touched a jellyfish!" Mom said. "You should never touch a jellyfish. They are very dangerous."

Dad picked up Sam and carried him to the car. He said, "We have to go to the doctor. He will make your hand better."

Mia followed them and felt sorry for Sam. She said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I tried to tell you not to touch it. I recognize the jellyfish because I saw it in a book. It is a broken jellyfish. It came out of the water and died on the sand. That is why it is here."

Sam nodded and said, "It's okay, Mia. I'm sorry, too. I should have listened to you. You are a smart sister. I will never touch a jellyfish again."

Tom and Lily were going to see a show with their mom and dad. They were very happy and excited. They liked to see people sing and dance on the stage. The stage was big and bright and had many colors.

When they got to the theater, they found their seats and waited for the show to start. Mom and dad told them to be quiet and polite. Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They wanted to be good and have fun.

But soon, Tom started to feel bored. He did not like the show. He thought it was too long and too loud and not interesting. He wanted to go home and play with his toys. He started to whine and fidget. He said, "Mom, I don't like this show. Can we go now?"

Mom tried to calm him down and said, "No, Tom, we have to stay until the end. The show is almost over. Please be patient and try to enjoy it. Look, Lily is having a good time. She likes the show. She thinks it is interesting."

But Tom did not listen. He got more and more upset. He started to cry and scream. He said, "No, no, no! I hate this show! I want to go home! I want to go home!" He made a lot of noise and disturbed the people around them.

Lily felt embarrassed and sad. She liked the show. She thought it was interesting. She wanted to watch it until the end. She did not like Tom's crying and screaming. She said, "Tom, please stop. You are being rude and mean. You are ruining the show for everyone. You are making me sad."

But Tom did not stop. He kept crying and screaming. Mom and dad had no choice. They had to take him out of the theater. They apologized to the people and left. Lily had to go with them. She did not get to see the end of the show. She felt very disappointed and angry. She did not talk to Tom for the rest of the day.

Lily and Ben were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were spies and look for clues. Lily saw a big envelope on the table. She picked it up and opened it. Inside, there were many papers with strange marks on them.

"Look, Ben, I found a secret message!" Lily said.

Ben ran over to see. He tried to read the papers, but he did not know what they meant. He saw some pictures of people and places. He pointed to one of them and said, "This is Grandma and Grandpa. They live far away."

Lily nodded. She remembered Grandma and Grandpa. They were very nice, but they could not hear very well. They were deaf. They used their hands to talk. Lily and Ben tried to learn their hand talk, but it was hard.

"Maybe this is a letter from Grandma and Grandpa," Lily said. "Maybe they want to see us."

"Or maybe it is a clue for a spy mission," Ben said. "Maybe they need our help."

They heard a knock on the door. They hid the envelope under a pillow and ran to see who it was. It was Mom and Dad. They had big smiles on their faces.

"Guess what, kids?" Mom said. "We have a surprise for you. We are going to visit Grandma and Grandpa for the weekend!"

Lily and Ben were very happy. They hugged Mom and Dad. They ran to get their bags and the envelope. They wanted to show Grandma and Grandpa their secret message. They did not know that the envelope was actually a tax return that Mom and Dad had to mail. They did not care. They only cared about seeing Grandma and Grandpa and having fun. They seemed very excited.

Lily wanted to buckle her own seat belt. She was a big girl now and she could do it by herself. She grabbed the buckle and tried to fit it into the slot. But it was hard. The buckle was too big or the slot was too small. She pushed and pulled and twisted and turned, but it did not work.

"Let me help you, Lily," Mom said. She reached over and took the buckle from Lily's hand. "You have to line it up like this and then click it in."

"No, Mom, I can do it!" Lily said. She was persistent. She wanted to buckle her own seat belt. She snatched the buckle back from Mom and tried again. But it was still hard. The buckle and the slot did not want to be friends.

"Lily, please, we have to go," Mom said. She was getting impatient. She had to drive Lily to preschool and then go to work. She did not have time for this. "Let me buckle you in and then you can try again later."

"No, Mom, I can do it!" Lily said. She was stubborn. She did not give up. She kept trying to fit the buckle into the slot. She did not care that Mom was waiting or that they were late. She only cared about buckling her own seat belt.

Finally, after many tries, Lily did it. She fit the buckle into the slot and heard a click. She smiled and clapped her hands. She was proud. She had buckled her own seat belt.

"Good job, Lily!" Mom said. She was relieved and happy. She praised Lily and gave her a hug. "You did it by yourself. You are a big girl now."

"Yes, Mom, I did it!" Lily said. She was excited and happy. She hugged Mom back and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you."

"I love you too, Lily," Mom said. She started the car and drove to preschool. She was glad that Lily was persistent and learned how to buckle her own seat belt. She hoped that Lily would also learn how to be patient and listen to Mom.

Lily liked to play with her dolls and have tea parties. She had a small table and chairs, and a pink tea set with cups and a pot. She also had a big bear that she called Ted, and he was her best friend.

One day, Lily decided to make tea for Ted and herself. She went to the kitchen and asked her mom for some water. Her mom smiled and gave her a jug of water. She said, "Be careful, Lily. Don't spill the water or burn yourself. The water is mild, not hot, but you still need to be careful."

Lily thanked her mom and carried the jug to her room. She put it on the table and poured some water into the pot. Then she filled two cups with water and pretended it was tea. She added some sugar and milk from her toy boxes. She said, "Here you go, Ted. This is your tea. It is mild and sweet, just like you."

She gave one cup to Ted and held the other one in her hand. She lifted it to her mouth and sipped. She made a slurping sound and said, "Mmm, this is good tea. Do you like it, Ted?"

Ted did not answer, because he was a bear and could not talk. But Lily knew he liked it, because he smiled with his eyes and nodded his head. She smiled back and said, "I'm glad you like it, Ted. You are my best friend. Let's have more tea and cookies."

Lily and Ben were scared of the big storm. It was a hurricane, their mom said. It made loud noises and broke things outside. Their mom told them to stay in the basement with her and their dad. They had flashlights, blankets, and snacks.

"Mom, will the storm go away?" Lily asked.

"Yes, sweetie, it will. But we have to wait until it is safe," mom said.

"Will our house be okay?" Ben asked.

"I hope so, honey. But don't worry, we have each other and we have help," mom said.

She hugged them and pointed to the radio. It was a reliable radio, their dad said. It could provide them with information and music. It had batteries that lasted a long time.

"Listen, the radio says the storm is getting weaker. That's good news," dad said.

He turned the knob and found a song they liked. He sang along and made them laugh.

Lily and Ben felt a little better. They cuddled with their mom and dad and listened to the radio. They hoped the storm would end soon and they could see their friends and their toys again. They were glad they had a reliable radio and a family that loved them.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and cars. Today, they want to make a big tower with blocks. They find many blocks in the toy box and start to build.

"Look, Anna, I have a blue block. It is very important for the tower. It is the top block," Ben says.

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to give the blue block. He likes the blue block. He says, "No, Anna, please let me keep the blue block. I want to put it on the red block."

Lily and Ben were very scared and sorry. They realized they had made a big mistake. They did not succeed in having fun. They only succeeded in getting into trouble. They wished they had listened to their mom. They wished they had been more humble and careful.

He told them to get back on their boat and row to the shore. He told them to never come near his ship again. He told them to be good and obey their mom. He told them to learn from their mistake and be humble and wise. He waved his hook and said goodbye.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the park and look at the birds and flowers. One day, they saw a big poster on a wall. It said: "Firework Show Tonight! Come and Watch the Sky Light Up!"

Lily and Sam wanted to see the firework show. They asked their moms if they could go. Their moms said yes, but they had to be careful and stay close to them. Fireworks were loud and bright and could hurt them if they were not careful.

That night, Lily and Sam went to the park with their moms. They saw many people and heard music and laughter. They found a good spot to watch the sky. They waited for the firework show to start.

Soon, they heard a loud boom and saw a flash of red and green. Then another boom and a flash of blue and yellow. Lily and Sam clapped and cheered. They liked the firework show. It was pretty and fun.

But then, they saw a boy near them. He had a firework in his hand. He looked at Lily and Sam and said: "Do you dare to light this firework? It will make a bigger boom and flash than those ones."

Lily and Sam shook their heads. They did not want to light the firework. They knew it was dangerous and wrong. They said: "No, we don't dare. You should not do that either. It is not safe. You could get hurt or hurt someone else. That is not a good way to have fun. That is serious."

The boy laughed and said: "You are scaredy-cats. I am not scared. I am brave. Watch me." He lit the firework and threw it in the air.

But he did not throw it far enough. The firework came down and landed near him. It exploded and made a loud boom and a flash of sparks. The boy screamed and ran away. He had burned his hand and his hair.

Lily and Sam were scared and sad. They hoped the boy was okay. They hugged their moms and said: "We are sorry, mom. We did not want to see that. We are glad we did not dare to light the firework. We are glad we listened to you. We love you, mom."

Their moms hugged them back and said: "We love you too, Lily and Sam. You are good and smart. You did the right thing. Fireworks are beautiful, but they are also dangerous. You have to be careful and respectful. You have to follow the rules and listen to the adults. That is how you have fun and stay safe."

One day, a fox and his friend came to visit the rabbit. The fox asked: "What can you do?" The rabbit gathered all his courage and said loudly: "I can speak!" His answer surprised everyone.

Suddenly, the fox laughed. He said: "Yes! I believe you can, but you need a tail to do it." The rabbit was sad and couldn't believe it.

But then, the fox said: "Don't worry, I have an idea. You can borrow my tail for a day and see if it works." The rabbit loved this plan and was very excited. He thanked the fox and put on the tail.

To everyone's surprise, the rabbit started talking immediately! He was now able to speak and everyone cheered. The fox was so proud of the humble rabbit and they all celebrated together.

The fox was persistent in keeping Hop away. Hop still wanted to explore the meadow, but he was too scared to go anywhere near the trap. He was very sad and stayed inside his burrow all the time.

Sara nodded and skipped along the sidewalk. She loved the park, with its swings and slides and sandbox. She saw some other kids playing and ran to join them. She saw a boy with a blue hat and a shovel. She wanted to play with the shovel, so she grabbed it from his hand.

"Hey, that's mine!" the boy cried. He tried to get the shovel back, but Sara held on tight. "Give it back, give it back!"

"No, it's mine now!" Sara said. She liked the shovel, it was shiny and big. She didn't want to share.

The boy started to weep. He was sad and angry. He wanted his shovel back. He ran to his mom and told her what happened. His mom came over and talked to Sara's mom.

Sara's mom was not happy. She looked at Sara and said, "Sara, that was not nice. You can't take things from other people without asking. How would you feel if someone took your hat?"

Sara thought about it. She loved her hat, it was her favorite. She would be very sad and angry if someone took it. She looked at the boy, who was still weeping. She felt sorry for him. She realized she had been mean.

She walked over to the boy and gave him back his shovel. She said, "I'm sorry, I shouldn't have taken your shovel. Do you want to play with me?"

The boy looked at her and wiped his tears. He smiled and said, "Okay, thank you. Do you want to play with my hat?"

Sara smiled and said, "Yes, please. Your hat is very nice. Do you want to play with my hat?"

They exchanged hats and played together in the sandbox. They had fun and became friends. Sara learned to share and be kind. Mom was proud of her.

Humble Owl lived in a big tree. He liked to help his friends in the forest. He was good at finding things and making sounds.

One day, he saw Little Mouse looking for his nut. Little Mouse had lost his nut and was very sad. Humble Owl flew down and said, "Hello, Little Mouse. Do you need help?"

"Yes, please, Humble Owl. I can't find my nut. I put it under a leaf, but now it is gone," said Little Mouse.

Humble Owl nodded and said, "Don't worry, Little Mouse. I will help you find your nut. Let's look around the tree."

They looked around the tree, but they could not find the nut. Humble Owl thought hard and said, "Maybe someone took your nut. Who likes nuts in the forest?"

Little Mouse thought and said, "Sneaky Squirrel likes nuts. He always takes nuts from other animals. Maybe he took my nut."

Humble Owl said, "Let's go and see Sneaky Squirrel. Maybe he has your nut."

They flew and ran to Sneaky Squirrel's hole. They saw Sneaky Squirrel eating a nut. It was Little Mouse's nut!

"Hey, Sneaky Squirrel, that is my nut! You took it from me!" said Little Mouse.

Sneaky Squirrel looked up and said, "No, it is not. It is my nut. I found it under a leaf. Go away!"

Humble Owl said, "That is not true, Sneaky Squirrel. Little Mouse put his nut under a leaf. You took it from him. That is not nice. You should give it back."

Sneaky Squirrel said, "No, I won't. It is mine. You can't make me."

Humble Owl said, "Yes, we can. We have many friends in the forest. They will help us. They don't like you, because you are greedy and mean. They like us, because we are kind and humble. If you don't give back the nut, we will tell them. They will come and make you sorry."

Sneaky Squirrel was scared. He knew Humble Owl was right. He did not want to make the other animals angry. He said, "Fine, fine. Here, take your nut. I don't want it anyway. Just leave me alone."

He threw the nut to Little Mouse and ran into his hole. Little Mouse was happy. He thanked Humble Owl and said, "You are the best, Humble Owl. You helped me get my nut back. You are very smart and brave."

Humble Owl smiled and said, "You are welcome, Little Mouse. I am glad you have your nut. You are very sweet and friendly."

They hugged and went back to their homes. They were happy and proud. They were good friends.

She sang happy songs and sad songs, loud songs and soft songs, old songs and new songs. But she had no one to sing with. She had no friends, no family, no pets. She wished she had someone to listen to her songs and sing with her.

One day, she heard a knock on her door. She opened it and saw a little girl. The little girl had a big smile and a red dress. She held a basket of flowers.

"Hello, Lonely Lady," the little girl said. "I am Lily. I live in the next street. I brought you some flowers. They are pretty and smell nice. Do you like them?"

Lonely Lady was surprised and happy. She took the flowers and thanked the little girl. She invited her to come inside.

"I sing because I love to sing, Lily. Singing makes me happy. But you are right, I also sing because I am lonely. I have no one to sing with. I have no one to talk to. I have no one to hug. I wish I had a friend like you."

Lonely Lady felt a warm feeling in her heart. She squeezed Lily's hand and nodded.

"Yes, Lily. You can be my friend. You are my friend. You make me happy. You make me not lonely. Thank you, Lily."

Lily hugged Lonely Lady and kissed her cheek.

"You are welcome, Lonely Lady. You are my friend. You make me happy. You make me not lonely. Can we sing together?"

"Yes, Lily. We can sing together. We can sing any song you want. What song do you want to sing?"

"I want to sing a song about friendship. A song that says we are friends forever. Do you know a song like that?"

Lonely Lady thought for a moment. Then she said:

"I do know a song like that. It is a song my mother used to sing to me when I was little. It is a song that says you are my sunshine, my only sunshine. You make me happy when skies are gray. Do you know that song?"

Lily nodded. She said:

"I do know that song. It is a song my father used to sing to me when I was little. It is a song that says you'll never know, dear, how much I love you. Please don't take my sunshine away. Can we sing that song?"

Lonely Lady nodded. She said:

"We can sing that song. We can sing it together. We can sing it loud and proud. We can sing it to the world. Are you ready?"

Lily nodded. She said:

"I am ready. Let's sing."

"Let's try to open it," Sue says.

They look for a key, but they do not find one. They see a window above the door. The window is small and high. They see a chair and a table near the door.

"Maybe we can climb on the chair and the table and reach the window," Tim says.

"OK, let's try," Sue says.

They move the chair and the table to the door. They climb on the chair and then on the table. The table is old and weak. It makes a noise. They do not care. They want to see the window.

Tim stands on the table and pushes the window. The window is stuck. He pushes harder. The window opens. He sees dust and dark and nothing else.

"Is there anything?" Sue asks.

"No, just dust and dark," Tim says.

He leans out of the window to see more. He loses his balance. He falls out of the window. He screams.

Sue screams too. She sees Tim fall. She sees blood and pain and fear.

She cries. She does not know what to do. She is alone in the old house. She is scared. She wants her mom and dad. She wants Tim. She wants to go home.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. But sometimes they make a big mess. Mommy is not happy when she sees the mess.

"Look at this, Sara and Tom!" Mommy says. "You have to clean your toys. They are all over the floor. You can trip and hurt yourself. And the toys can get dirty and broken."

"But Mommy, we are having fun!" Sara says. "We don't want to clean now. We want to play more."

"Me too!" Tom says. "Cleaning is boring. Playing is fun."

Mommy sighs. She sees a gray cat sitting on the couch. The cat is watching Sara and Tom. The cat is Mommy's friend. She is very useful. She helps Mommy catch mice and bugs.

"Maybe you can learn from the cat," Mommy says. "She is very good at cleaning herself. She licks her fur every day. She keeps herself nice and neat. She is a smart and tidy cat."

Sara and Tom look at the cat. They see how she washes her face and paws with her tongue. They think she is cute and clever.

"Wow, the cat is very good at cleaning!" Sara says. "She is a useful cat. Maybe we can be useful too."

"Yeah, maybe we can," Tom says. "Maybe we can clean our toys and make Mommy happy. And then we can play with the cat. She is fun too."

Sara and Tom nod. They start to pick up their toys and put them in the box. Mommy smiles. She is proud of Sara and Tom. She gives them a hug and a kiss.

"Thank you, Sara and Tom," Mommy says. "You are very good at cleaning. You are very useful. And you are very sweet. I love you."

"I love you too, Mommy," Sara and Tom say. "And we love the cat. She is our friend. She is a gray and useful cat."

Ben was a brave boy who liked to play with his toy weapon. It was a big stick with a star on the end. He pretended it was a sword and he was a knight. He had a furry hat that looked like a lion's mane. He wore it when he went on adventures.

One night, he had a bad dream. He saw a scary monster with big teeth and claws. It wanted to eat him. He tried to run away, but the monster was faster. He shouted for help, but no one heard him. He was very afraid.

He woke up with a start. He felt his heart beating fast and his face wet with tears. He looked around and saw his room. He saw his toy weapon and his furry hat on the floor. He felt better. He reached for them and hugged them.

He heard a knock on the door. It was his mom. She opened the door and saw him. She smiled and came to his bed. She asked him, "What's wrong, Ben? Did you have a bad dream?"

Ben nodded and told her about the monster. He showed her his toy weapon and his furry hat. He said, "These are my friends. They protect me from the monster."

His mom hugged him and kissed him. She said, "You are very brave, Ben. But you don't need to be afraid of monsters. They are not real. They are only in your head. And you have me and dad and your sister. We love you and we will always keep you safe."

Ben felt better. He smiled and said, "I love you too, mom. Can I sleep with my toy weapon and my furry hat?"

His mom said, "Of course, you can. They are your special things. But remember, the best weapon is your heart. And the best hat is your smile."

Ben nodded and snuggled with his mom. He closed his eyes and fell asleep. He dreamed of happy things. He did not see the monster again.

Tom and Jen were twins who liked to play with rocks. They had a big box of rocks of different shapes and colors. One day, they found a shiny rock that was red and brown. They thought it was very impressive.

"Look, Jen, this rock is so pretty!" Tom said, holding the rock in his hand.

"Can I see it, Tom?" Jen asked, reaching for the rock.

"No, it's mine! I found it first!" Tom said, pulling the rock away.

Jen was angry. She wanted the rock too. She saw another rock on the floor. It was hard and gray. She picked it up and threw it at Tom.

"Ow!" Tom cried, as the rock hit his head. He dropped the shiny rock and held his head. Blood came out of his head.

Jen was scared. She did not mean to hurt Tom. She ran to the shiny rock and picked it up. She wanted to give it to Tom and say sorry.

But before she could do that, she heard a loud noise. It was their dad. He had come home from work. He saw the blood and the rock and got very angry.

"What have you done?" he yelled, grabbing the rock from Jen. "This is not a rock, this is copper! It is very valuable! You could have sold it for a lot of money! But you wasted it by throwing it at your brother! You are very bad!"

He threw the copper on the floor and hit Jen with his hand. Jen cried and fell down. Tom cried too. He tried to help Jen, but his head hurt too much.

Their dad did not care. He left them alone and went to his room. He locked the door and did not come out.

Tom and Jen were very sad. They wished they had never found the copper. They wished they had shared it and played with it nicely. They wished their dad was nice too. But it was too late. They had made a big mistake. And they had to pay for it.

Tom is a boy who likes to play with his toys. He has a car, a ball, a bear and a doll. He likes to make noises with his toys and pretend they are alive.

One day, he is playing in his room when he hears a loud knock on the door. He stops playing and looks at the door. He hears a voice say, "Hello, I am the man who fixes the pipes. Can I come in?"

Tom is scared. He does not know the man. The man has no hair on his head. He is bald. Tom thinks the man is bad. He hides under his bed and holds his bear.

The man opens the door and sees Tom's toys on the floor. He smiles and says, "What nice toys you have. Do you want to show me how you play with them?"

Tom does not answer. He does not want to talk to the man. He does not want the man to touch his toys. He hopes the man will go away.

The man walks to the bed and looks under it. He sees Tom and his bear. He says, "Don't be afraid, little boy. I am not here to hurt you. I am here to help you. Your pipes are broken and I need to fix them. Do you know where they are?"

Tom shakes his head. He does not know where the pipes are. He does not care about the pipes. He only cares about his toys and his bear. He wishes his mom or dad were here.

The man says, "It's okay. I will find the pipes myself. You can stay here and play with your toys. But please don't make too much noise. I need to hear the water and the tools."

The man leaves the room and closes the door. Tom hears him go to the bathroom and the kitchen. He hears him bang and twist and turn. He hears the water run and stop.

Tom is still scared. He does not like the noise. He does not like the man. He wants the man to leave. He hugs his bear and waits.

He wishes he could play with his dad again. But he cannot. He has to stay in his room. He has to be alone. He has no laptop. He has no pages. He has no fun. He has an empty day.

Sara and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They had a favorite swing that was big and red and went very high. But one day, when they came to the park, they saw that the swing was broken. Someone had cut the rope and the seat was on the ground.

"Who did this?" Sara asked, feeling sad and angry. "They spoiled our swing!"

"I don't know," Ben said, looking around. "Maybe it was the big kids who are always mean and loud. They don't like to share."

Sara and Ben wanted to restore their swing, but they didn't know how. They tried to tie the rope back together, but it was too short and weak. They tried to find another seat, but they couldn't find anything that fit. They felt like giving up.

Then they saw Mr. Lee, the park keeper, walking by with his tools. He was a kind and friendly man who always said hello to them. Sara and Ben ran to him and told him what happened.

"Oh, that's terrible," Mr. Lee said, shaking his head. "Some people have no respect for other people's things. Don't worry, I'll help you restore your swing. I have some extra rope and a new seat in my truck. Come on, let's go get them."

Sara and Ben followed Mr. Lee to his truck and helped him carry the rope and the seat to the swing. Mr. Lee used his tools to cut the old rope and attach the new one. He also fixed the hook and the chain that held the seat. He lifted the seat and hung it on the swing.

"There you go," he said, smiling. "Your swing is good as new. You can try it now."

Sara and Ben thanked Mr. Lee and hugged him. They were so happy to see their swing restored. They took turns pushing each other and flying high in the air. They laughed and shouted with joy. They forgot about the big kids who spoiled their swing. They only thought about their friend who helped them.

Sam and Ben liked to build things with their blocks. They made houses, towers, bridges, and cars. They had a lot of fun playing together.

One day, they found a long, thin rope in the garage. It was black and shiny, and it had a handle at one end. Sam picked it up and said, "Look, Ben, I have a whip! I can be a mighty cowboy and whip the bad guys!"

Ben was curious and wanted to try the whip too. He said, "Can I have a turn, Sam? Please?"

Sam said, "No, it's mine! I found it first!" He swung the whip in the air and made a loud crack. He laughed and said, "See? I'm the best whipper in the world!"

Ben was sad and angry. He said, "That's not fair, Sam! You have to share! Give me the whip, or I'll knock down your blocks!"

Sam said, "No, you won't! I'll whip you if you touch my blocks!" He ran to his block tower and stood in front of it.

Ben said, "Yes, I will! Watch me!" He ran to the block tower and pushed it with his hands. The blocks fell down and made a big mess.

Sam was very mad. He said, "You're a meanie, Ben! You broke my tower!" He raised the whip and tried to hit Ben with it.

But he was not careful. He whipped too hard and too fast. The whip slipped out of his hand and flew in the air. It landed on the shelf where Dad kept his tools. It knocked down a big hammer that was on the edge.

The hammer fell down and hit Sam on the head. Sam cried out and fell to the floor. He had a big bump on his head.

Ben was scared. He said, "Oh no, Sam! Are you okay? I'm sorry, I'm sorry!"

He ran to Sam and hugged him. He said, "I didn't mean to make you hurt, Sam. I just wanted to play with the whip too. Can we be friends again?"

Sam was in pain, but he was also sorry. He said, "I'm okay, Ben. I'm sorry too. I should have shared the whip with you. It was not nice to keep it all to myself. Can we be friends again?"

Ben said, "Yes, we can. I love you, Sam."

Sam said, "I love you too, Ben."

They hugged each other and said they were sorry. They decided to put the whip back where they found it and never play with it again. They cleaned up the blocks and the hammer and went to Mom. She gave them a kiss and a band-aid and said they were good boys. They smiled and said they were happy. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharing is caring, and that whips are not toys.

"Tom, don't cry. I have a plan. We can cut off the messy part of the cake and put it on a plate. Then we can flip the cake back and put it in the fridge. Maybe Mom won't notice."

But Sara did notice. When they got to the beach, she opened her bag and saw that her doll was gone. She was very sad and angry. She looked at Ben's bag and saw a lump that looked like her doll. She opened his bag and found her doll inside. She shouted at Ben.

"Ben, you are naughty! You took my doll without asking! You did not borrow, you stole! That is not nice! Give me back my doll!"

Ben felt ashamed. He knew he did wrong. He gave Sara back her doll and said sorry.

"Sara, I am sorry. I was naughty. I wanted to play with your doll, but I should have asked you first. I did not borrow, I stole. That is not nice. Can you forgive me?"

Sara was still upset, but she saw that Ben was sorry. She decided to forgive him. She hugged him and said.

"Ben, I forgive you. You are my brother and I love you. But next time, you have to ask me before you take my things. That is how you borrow. And maybe we can share our toys sometimes. That is how we can be nice to each other."

Ben nodded and hugged her back. He said.

"Sara, thank you. You are my sister and I love you. Next time, I will ask you before I take your things. That is how I borrow. And maybe we can share our toys sometimes. That is how we can be nice to each other."

Mom and dad saw them and smiled. They were proud of their twins. They said.

"Sara and Ben, you are good children. You learned a lesson today. Borrowing is when you ask someone to use their things and give them back. Stealing is when you take someone's things without asking and keep them. Borrowing is nice, stealing is naughty. Sharing is also nice, because it shows you care. We are happy that you are nice to each other. Now let's have fun on our holiday!"

Sara and Ben agreed. They played with their toys and with each other. They had fun on their holiday. They learned to borrow, not to steal, and to share. They were happy.

On a mild morning, she opened her eyes and saw a beautiful lamp just next to her bed. She jumped up and switched it on. A cosy orange light filled the room and she could see colourful shapes on her walls. The light felt warm and comforting. 

The little girl smiled and started to imagine all the fun she would have that day. She got out of bed and ran around her room. She loved the warm, mild light from the lamp that gave off a magical feeling.

The little girl's days were always filled with laughter and joy, thanks to the special lamp in her room. It reminded her to stay positive and enjoy every day.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to race each other. They raced on their bikes, on their feet, and on their slides. One day, they saw a big pear tree in the park. It had many ripe pears that looked yummy.

"Let's race to the pear tree and see who can pick the most pears!" Max said.

"OK, but be careful. The pears are delicate and can break easily," Lily said.

They ran as fast as they could to the pear tree. Max got there first and started to grab the pears. He did not care if he hurt them or dropped them. Lily got there second and picked the pears gently. She put them in her basket.

"Ha! I have more pears than you!" Max said.

"But look, your pears are all bruised and squished. Mine are still nice and smooth," Lily said.

She showed him her basket. Max looked at his pears and felt sad. He wished he had been more careful.

"I'm sorry, Lily. You are right. I was too rough with the pears. Can we share them?" he asked.

Lily smiled and nodded. She gave him some of her pears and took some of his. They sat under the pear tree and ate the pears together. They agreed that they were both good at racing, but they also needed to be gentle with the things they loved.

Lily and Max were playing in their room. They had many toys, but they liked to use other things too. Lily found a hanger in the closet. She thought it was funny and shiny. She wanted to poke Max with it.

"Hey, Max, look at this!" she said, and poked him in the arm.

"Ow, Lily, that hurts!" Max said, and pushed her away.

Lily did not like that. She poked him again, harder.

"Stop it, Lily, or I'll tell Mom!" Max said, and grabbed the hanger.

They both pulled on the hanger. It was rare and old. It belonged to their grandma. It was not strong. It broke in two.

"Oh no, what have we done?" Lily said, and started to cry.

Max felt bad too. He hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I should not have pushed you. But you should not have poked me. It was not nice."

They heard Mom coming. They were scared. They did not want to get in trouble. They hid the broken hanger under the bed.

Mom came in and saw them. She smiled and said, "What are you two doing? Are you having fun?"

Lily and Max looked at each other. They knew they had to tell the truth. They said, "Mom, we're sorry. We broke the hanger. It was grandma's. We were playing and fighting. We did not mean to."

Mom looked sad. She said, "Oh, kids, that was a rare and special hanger. Grandma gave it to me when I was little. It was very precious to me. Why did you play with it?"

Lily and Max felt sorry. They said, "We did not know, Mom. We thought it was just a hanger. We were bored and curious. We will not do it again."

Mom sighed and said, "I know, kids. I know you did not mean to hurt me or the hanger. But you have to be careful with other people's things. You have to ask before you touch them. And you have to be kind to each other. Poking and pushing is not fun. It is mean and dangerous. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We're sorry. We love you."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too, kids. I forgive you. But you have to help me fix the hanger. And you have to play nicely from now on. OK?"

Lily and Max said, "OK, Mom. Thank you."

They learned their lesson. They never poked or pushed each other again. They respected other people's things. And they played happily with their toys.

Anna liked to help her mom bake. She liked to crack the eggs, pour the milk, and stir the flour. But her favorite thing was to use the mixer. The mixer was big and shiny and made a loud noise. It made the batter smooth and fluffy.

"Can I use the mixer, mom?" Anna asked.

Mom gave Anna the mixer and plugged it in. Anna held it with both hands and pressed the button. The mixer whirred and spun. Anna felt it shake and pull. She smiled and moved it around the bowl.

"Look, mom, I'm mixing!" Anna said.

"You're doing great, sweetie. Just a little more and we're done," mom said.

Anna wanted to make the batter even smoother. She lifted the mixer a little bit and moved it faster. She didn't see the orange peel that mom had left on the counter. The mixer hit the peel and slipped out of Anna's hands. It flew across the kitchen and hit the wall. The batter splattered everywhere. Anna gasped and mom screamed.

"Oh no, Anna, what have you done?" mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom, I didn't mean to. The mixer was too strong. It hit the orange and it passed me," Anna said.

Mom looked at the mess and sighed. She unplugged the mixer and picked it up. She checked if it was broken. It wasn't. She hugged Anna and said, "It's okay, honey, accidents happen. But next time, please be more careful with the mixer. And don't lift it out of the bowl. And watch out for the orange peels."

"I will, mom, I promise. Can we still bake the cake?" Anna asked.

"Of course we can, sweetie. We just have to clean up first. And maybe add some more flour. And some orange zest. It will make the cake taste better," mom said.

Anna smiled and helped mom clean up. She learned her lesson. She liked to use the mixer, but she liked to bake with mom more.

After a while, Ben found a note under a big tree. The note said, "This stone is magic! Make a wish and see what happens!" Ben and his friends made wishes and passed the stone around. To their surprise, their wishes came true! They were all very happy and played with the magic stone all day long.

But as they walked, they reached an area much more dangerous than they'd expected. Mama and Papa stopped and tried to figure out what to do. Suddenly Papa had an idea. He picked up a stick and waved it in the air. Then he yelled in a loud voice, "Surrender!" 

Nobody answered. After a moment, Mama and Papa laughed. They continued walking and soon they made it out of the dangerous woods. 

When they got home, Mama started making pasta for dinner. She put the pasta in boiling water and added some yummy spices. She let it cook for a few minutes, then declared it ready.

Mama and Papa ate the delicious pasta and thanked the woods for offering up its excitement. But that night, they decided to never go into the dangerous woods again!

The sun smiled down on the bunny and the butter. When the bunny woke up, the butter had melted away! The bunny was sad. It wanted to play in the butter again, but it was gone.

The bunny made a wish that the butter would come back. The next morning, the bunny woke up and the butter was back again! The bunny smiled as it released all the butter across the ground again. The bunny was so happy, it stopped being tired and hopped around in the butter all day, playing and having a lot of fun.

But then, another boy came. He said, "No, that's my wallet!" The man and the boy both wanted the wallet. They did not know what to do. Tim thought for a moment. He asked them both, "What is inside the wallet?"

The man said, "There is a photo of my family." The boy said, "There are two coins in it." Tim opened the wallet and saw a photo and two coins. He gave the wallet to the man. The boy was sad, but Tim said, "Don't worry, we can all play together in the park!" And they all became friends.

Tim wanted to eat the prune, but he was too small to reach it. He saw a big stick on the ground. Tim thought he could use the stick to get the prune. He picked up the stick and tried to knock the prune off the tree. But a fierce dog came running and barked at Tim.

The dog scared Tim, but he did not give up. He waited for the dog to go away. When the dog left, Tim tried again with the stick. This time, he got the prune! Tim was so happy that he did not give up. He ate the prune and it was very sweet. Tim learned that even when things are hard, he should keep trying.

They both went to class and had a great day. After school, they went to the park and played on the swings. Suddenly, they saw a spoiled apple on the ground. Lily said, "Eww, that apple is spoiled. Let's not touch it." Emily agreed and they continued playing. They had a wonderful day together and promised to help each other whenever they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a penny that she loved to play with. One day, Lily was feeling very sleepy, so she decided to take a nap. But before she closed her eyes, she whispered to her penny, "Goodnight, my friend."

As she slept, her penny started to glow and spin. Suddenly, a magical fairy appeared! The fairy said to Lily, "Hello, sleepy girl. I am here to grant your wish. What would you like?"

Lily rubbed her eyes and looked at the fairy. She whispered, "I wish for a big, fluffy pillow to sleep on." The fairy smiled and waved her wand. In an instant, a soft pillow appeared under Lily's head.

Lily snuggled up with her penny and her new pillow, feeling very happy and grateful. She whispered to her penny, "Thank you for being my friend and for helping me get a good night's sleep." And with that, she drifted off into a peaceful slumber.

Once upon a time, there was a scared little pig. He was scared of the big, bad wolf. The wolf wanted to eat the pig, but the pig didn't want to be eaten. So, the pig went to find a safe place to settle down. 

The pig found a cozy house made of straw. He thought it would be a good place to hide from the wolf. But the wolf found the house and tried to blow it down. The pig was very scared, but he didn't give up. 

The pig ran to another house made of sticks. He thought it would be stronger than the straw house. But the wolf found this house too and tried to blow it down. The pig was still scared, but he didn't give up. 

Finally, the pig found a house made of bricks. It was very strong and the wolf couldn't blow it down. The pig felt safe and settled down in the brick house. He was no longer scared of the big, bad wolf.

That night, Emily's mom asked her about her day. Emily mentioned the special stone she found with Max. Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a fun day, Emily!" Emily agreed, and she and Max went to bed, excited for more adventures in their dull town in the big universe.

"Hello, Mr. Crab," said Tim. "What are you doing here?" The crab looked at Tim and said, "I am collecting shells before the tide comes in." Tim wanted to help the crab, so they looked for shells together.

They found many pretty shells. Some were big, some were small. Tim and the crab put the shells in a pile. The tide started to come in. The water got closer and closer. Tim and the crab had to move fast.

"Thank you for helping me, Tim," said the green crab. "Now we have many shells to take home." Tim was happy to help his new friend. They had fun collecting shells by the sea.

Buddy said to Tim, "Stay back, I will protect you." Tim knew Buddy would keep him safe. Buddy barked at the cat, and the cat hissed back. They knew the fight was about to begin.

Buddy and the cat fought for a little while. Buddy was strong and brave. In the end, Buddy won, and the cat ran away. Tim hugged Buddy and said, "Thank you for protecting me, Buddy. You are the best dog ever!" They went home, happy and safe, knowing that they would always be there for each other.

Tom told the little girl, "I can fix your toy." The girl was happy. Tom took the toy and began to fix it. He worked hard and soon the toy was like new. The girl was very happy, but Tom knew that something else was going to happen.

Later that day, Tom heard a loud noise. It was a big fire! Tom put on his fancy red hat and went to put out the fire. He was brave and strong. He saved the day, just like he fixed the little girl's toy. The people in the town were so happy, and they knew that Tom the fireman would always help them.

"I don't know where I belong in the sky," said Twinkle. "There are so many stars, and I don't know where to go."

Luna smiled and said, "I can help you sort it out. Let's find the best place for you to shine."

So, Luna and Twinkle went through the sky, looking at all the stars. They found a spot where there were not many stars. Luna said, "This is the perfect place for you, Twinkle."

Twinkle was happy and started to shine brightly in her new spot. She was not worried anymore. She knew she belonged in the sky, and she had a new friend in Luna. They lived happily ever after, lighting up the night sky together.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play on the beach. They made sand castles and dug holes and looked for shells. One day, they saw a big fat crab walking on the sand. They wanted to catch it and put it in their bucket.

"Look, a crab!" Tim said. "Let's get it!"

They ran after the crab, but it was fast and clever. It hid under a rock and then ran to another one. Tim and Sam followed it, but they did not see that the tide was coming in. The water was getting higher and higher.

"Stop, stop!" Sam said. "The tide is coming! We have to go back!"

But Tim did not listen. He wanted to catch the crab. He reached for it, but it pinched his finger. He cried out in pain and dropped the crab. The crab ran away and the water covered it.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tim said. "The crab bit me!"

He looked around and saw that the water was very deep. He was scared and he could not see the beach. He started to cry.

"Help, help!" he shouted.

Sam heard him and swam to him. He grabbed his hand and pulled him to the shore. They were wet and cold and tired. Their mother was waiting for them. She was angry and worried.

"Where were you?" she said. "I told you to stay close to me! The tide is dangerous! You could have drowned!"

She hugged them and dried them with a towel. She checked Tim's finger and put a band-aid on it.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Tim said. "I wanted to catch the crab, but it was mean and it hurt me."

"I'm sorry, too, Mom," Sam said. "I tried to stop him, but he did not listen to me."

Mom smiled and kissed them.

"I'm glad you are safe," she said. "But you have to be careful on the beach. The tide can change quickly and the crabs can bite. You have to listen to me and to each other. Do you understand?"

Tim and Sam nodded.

"Yes, Mom," they said.

They learned their lesson. They never chased crabs again. They played on the beach, but they always watched the tide and stayed close to Mom. They had fun and they were happy.

One day, he saw a shiny pin on the floor. He thought it would be fun to play with it and add it to his tricks. He picked it up with his mouth and ran to his friends. "Look what I have!" he said. "I can make it spin and sparkle!"

His friends were curious and came closer. But then, Tommy felt a sharp pain in his tongue. He had bitten the pin by mistake and it hurt him a lot. He dropped the pin and cried out loud. "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts, it hurts!"

His friends were worried and tried to help him. They licked his tongue and comforted him. They told him to be careful with things he did not know. "Pins are not toys, Tommy," they said. "They are sharp and can hurt you. You should only play with safe things that are meant for cats."

Tommy learned his lesson. He was sorry for being silly and thanked his friends for being kind. He decided to perform only with his ball and his ribbon from then on. He realized that being a good friend was more important than being a good performer.

"Can we go near the ants?" Lily asks Ben.

"OK, but be careful. Ants can bite," Ben says.

They walk to the ant hill. They see many ants. Some ants are big and black. Some ants are small and red. The ants are busy. They carry food and dirt.

Lily and Ben watch the ants. They are curious. They want to know more.

"Where do the ants live?" Lily asks.

"They live in the ant hill. The ant hill is their home. It has many cells. Cells are small rooms for the ants," Ben says.

"How do you know that?" Lily asks.

"I read it in a book. Books have many words. Words tell you things," Ben says.

Lily nods. She likes books too. She wants to learn more words.

"Can we touch the ants?" Lily asks.

"No, we can't. That is not nice. The ants will be angry. They will bite us. Bites hurt," Ben says.

Lily frowns. She wants to touch the ants. She thinks they are soft and cute.

"I want to touch one ant. Just one. I will be brave. I will not be scared," Lily says.

She reaches out her hand. She picks up a small red ant. The ant is angry. It bites Lily's finger. Lily cries. It hurts.

"Ow, ow, ow! The ant bit me! It hurts!" Lily says.

Ben runs to Lily. He takes the ant from her hand. He puts it back on the ant hill. He hugs Lily.

"I told you not to touch the ants. They don't like that. You have to be gentle with animals. Animals have feelings too," Ben says.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I was not gentle. I was not smart. I was not brave. I was silly," Lily says.

She looks at her finger. It is red and swollen. She feels sorry for the ant too.

"Will the ant be OK?" Lily asks.

"I think so. The ant will go back to its cell. The cell is safe and warm. The ant will be with its friends. The ant will be happy," Ben says.

Lily smiles. She is glad the ant is OK. She is glad Ben is her friend. He is smart and kind. He is brave.

"Can we go back to the park?" Lily asks.

"OK, but no more touching ants. Let's play on the slide. The slide is fun," Ben says.

They hold hands. They walk to the slide. They play and laugh. They have fun.

Tom and Lily were playing in the old house. They liked to pretend they were explorers and find new things. They went up the stairs and saw a big door. They opened it and saw a dark room.

"Wow, look at all the stuff!" Tom said. He saw a big bed, a dusty mirror, and a lot of books. He ran to the bed and jumped on it.

Lily followed him and saw a picture on the wall. It was a man and a woman in old clothes. They looked happy and they were kissing.

"Who are they?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe they lived here a long time ago," Tom said. He got off the bed and went to the mirror. He wiped the dust with his hand and looked at himself. He made a funny face and laughed.

Lily went to the books and picked one up. She opened it and saw some words. She could not read them, but she liked the pictures. They were of animals and flowers and stars.

Suddenly, they heard a noise. It was like a whisper. They turned around and saw a white shape. It was a ghost!

The ghost looked at them and smiled. It was the woman from the picture. She floated to them and said, "Hello, children. I'm glad you came to visit. I've been lonely for a long time."

Tom and Lily were scared. They hugged each other and said, "Go away, ghost! You're scary!"

The ghost shook her head and said, "Don't be afraid. I won't hurt you. I just want to talk to you. You remind me of my children. They used to play here too, before they grew up and left."

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They felt sorry for the ghost. She seemed nice and sad.

"Where is your husband?" Lily asked.

The ghost pointed to the picture and said, "He's there. He died a long time ago. I miss him so much. He used to kiss me every day and tell me he loved me."

Tom and Lily felt more sorry for the ghost. They thought about their parents and how they loved them.

"Can we kiss you?" Tom asked.

The ghost smiled and said, "Yes, you can. That would make me very happy."

Tom and Lily went to the ghost and gave her a kiss on the cheek. The ghost felt warm and soft. She hugged them and said, "Thank you, children. You're very kind and brave. You made me feel less lonely."

Tom and Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, ghost. You're very unusual and nice. We're glad we met you."

The ghost smiled and said, "Me too. Now, you should go back to your parents. They might be worried about you. But you can come back and visit me anytime. I'll be waiting for you."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, ghost. We'll come back and see you. Goodbye, ghost."

The ghost said, "Goodbye, children. Have fun and be safe."

Tom and Lily took their hands and ran to the door. They looked back and saw the ghost waving at them. They waved back and left the room.

They went down the stairs and out of the house. They saw their parents waiting for them. They ran to them and hugged them.

"Where have you been?" their parents asked.

"We were playing in the old house," Tom and Lily said.

"Did you find anything interesting?" their parents asked.

Tom and Lily looked at each other and smiled. They said, "Yes, we did. We found a ghost."

One day, he heard a loud roar from the forest. He knew it was a dragon who wanted to burn the village. He grabbed his sword and shield and ran to the forest. He saw a big green dragon with red eyes and sharp teeth. The dragon saw him too and breathed fire at him.

Tom raised his shield to block the fire. The fire was very hot and made his shield wet. Tom felt the wetness on his arm and thought it was his sweat. He said to the dragon, "You cannot hurt me, dragon. My shield is too strong for you. Go away or I will cut you with my sword."

The dragon was angry and breathed fire again. Tom blocked it with his shield again. But this time, he saw something strange. His shield was not shiny anymore. It was black and smoky. The fire had burned his polish and made his shield dirty.

Tom was scared and sad. He liked his shiny shield. He did not want it to be dirty. He said to the dragon, "Please stop, dragon. You have ruined my shield. It was my favorite thing. Why are you so mean?"

The dragon heard Tom's words and felt sorry for him. He did not want to ruin Tom's shield. He was just hungry and looking for food. He said to Tom, "I am sorry, knight. The dragon nodded and said, "I promise, knight. I will not burn the village or eat the people. I will find other food in the forest. And I will help you clean your shield. Maybe I can polish it with my tail. It is very soft and smooth."

She ran to the gate and reached for the flower. But she did not see the bee that was on it. The bee was angry and stung her hand. Sara cried out loud and dropped the flower. It hurt a lot.

Tom heard her cry and ran to her. He saw the bee flying away and the flower on the ground. He saw Sara's hand was red and swollen. He felt sorry for her and hugged her.

"Are you okay, Sara?" he asked.

"No, it hurts. The bee was bad. It slapped me with its tail," Sara said.

Tom did not know what to say. He did not know that bees had tails. He thought they had stingers. But he did not want to make Sara more upset. He wanted to make her feel better.

He picked up the flower and gave it to her. He said, "Here, this is for you. It is a beautiful flower. You are a beautiful friend. I like you, Sara."

Sara smiled and took the flower. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a nice friend. I like you, too."

They held hands and walked back to the house. They asked Mom for some ice and a band-aid. Mom kissed Sara's hand and said, "You are brave, Sara. Bees can be mean sometimes. But they also make honey. Honey is sweet and good for you."

Sara and Tom nodded. They liked honey. They ate some honey and bread and felt better. They decided to play with their toys instead of the flowers. They did not want to meet any more bees. They had enough of slapping for one day.

Suddenly, Timmy's mommy appeared with an umbrella and said, "Come on, boys, let's go home before we get soaked!" Timmy and Johnny ran to the car, still laughing and whistling. They were so happy to have made a new friend who loved to whistle and joke just like they did.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her cozy bathrobe after bath time. One day, Lily's mom asked her to put away her toys. 

Lily didn't want to listen and said, "I don't want to clean up. I want to play!" 

Her mom replied, "Lily, it's important to clean up after ourselves. We don't want to be naughty and leave a mess." 

Lily thought about it and decided to raise her toys off the floor. She felt proud of herself for being a good listener. And after she was done, she put on her warm bathrobe and snuggled up with her favorite book.

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to play. He had a playful dog who liked to chase him around. One day, the man and his dog went to the park to play. They saw some other dogs and asked if they wanted to play too. 

But one of the dogs didn't want to play. He wanted to fight. The man and his dog didn't want to fight, but the other dog kept barking and growling. The man tried to talk to the other dog's owner, but they didn't listen. 

The man and his dog decided to leave and go play somewhere else. They didn't want to be near the mean dog who wanted to fight. They found a nice spot by the river and played fetch. The man was happy that he and his dog could play without any fighting.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Max. Max loved to play with his favorite ball. One day, Max's owner, Sarah, brought home a new toy for Max. It was a big red ball with a star symbol on it. Max was so excited to play with his new toy! 

But one day, Sarah was careless and left the gate open. Max saw the open gate and ran out to play. He chased his new ball all around the park. Suddenly, Max saw a squirrel and ran after it. He didn't turn back when Sarah called for him. 

Sarah was sad when Max didn't come back. She searched all over the park for him. Finally, she found Max playing with his new ball under a tree. Max was so happy to see Sarah and he turned his head to give her a big lick. From then on, Sarah was more careful and always made sure to close the gate.
