After diving, Blue flew around the city and saw many things. There were tall buildings, colorful flowers, and happy people walking around. Blue loved living in the lively city and diving into the pond.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he went to the lake with his mommy and daddy. They brought a small boat called a kayak.

Timmy was frightened at first because the water looked deep and scary. But then he saw how much fun his parents were having in the kayak. He wanted to try it too! So, he got in the kayak with his daddy and they paddled around the lake.

As they were exploring, they discovered a family of ducks swimming nearby. Timmy was so excited to see them up close. He shouted, "Quack quack!" and the ducks quacked back. It was a wonderful adventure that Timmy would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Tom. Tom loved to eat fish and sleep all day. One day, Tom went for a walk in the park and saw a little girl sitting on a bench. 

"Hello, little girl," said Tom. "What are you doing?"

"I'm listening to the silence," said the little girl.

"The silence?" asked Tom. "What is that?"

"It's when there's no sound," said the little girl.

Tom listened carefully and heard the silence too. "Wow," said Tom. "I never knew about the silence before. It's so peaceful."

From then on, Tom would often visit the little girl in the park to listen to the silence together. They would sit quietly and enjoy the peacefulness of the park. And even though Tom was a fat cat, he was happy to have a new friend who taught him about the beauty of silence.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she found a lime on the ground. It was green and round, and she thought it looked like a ball. She picked it up and threw it in the air, but it didn't bounce like a ball. It just rolled away.

As she was walking back to her house, she heard a quiet sound. It was her dog, Max, sleeping on the porch. Suddenly, Max woke up and sneezed really loud! Lily giggled and petted him. She loved her dog, even when he sneezed. 

That night, as Lily was getting ready for bed, she remembered the lime she found. She wondered if it tasted good. So, she asked her mom if she could try it. Her mom cut a small piece for her to taste. It was sour and made her scrunch up her face. But she was glad she tried it. From that day on, she always remembered the lime that made her dog sneeze.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice for dinner every night. One day, Lily's mom cooked some rice for her, but it was too hot. Lily tried to eat it, but it burned her tongue. She started to cry.

Lily's mom said, "Don't cry, Lily. It's okay. Let's wait for the rice to cool down. Then you can eat it calmly."

Lily stopped crying and waited for the rice to cool down. After a few minutes, she tried it again. This time, it was just right. Lily smiled and said, "This rice is yummy!"

Her mom replied, "I'm glad you like it. But remember, it's not good to lie. If you don't like something, it's okay to say so. We can always try something else." 

Lily nodded her head and said, "Okay, Mom. I'll tell you if I don't like something. But I really do like this rice!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and trucks. One day, Timmy and his mommy were walking outside when they saw a big, clean vehicle. Timmy gazed at the vehicle with wonder in his eyes.

"Mommy, can we go see the vehicle?" Timmy asked.

"Sure, let's go take a look," his mommy replied.

When they got closer, Timmy saw that the vehicle was a big, red fire truck. A firefighter was standing next to it.

"Hello there, little one. Do you like our truck?" the firefighter asked.

"Yes, it's so big and clean!" Timmy exclaimed.

The firefighter smiled and said, "We keep it clean so we can get to fires quickly and safely. Would you like to sit in the driver's seat?"

Timmy's eyes widened with excitement as he climbed up into the truck. "This is so cool!" he said.

As they walked away, Timmy turned to his mommy and said, "I want to be a firefighter when I grow up!"

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. Benny was very hungry and he wanted to eat a carrot. He looked everywhere for a carrot but he couldn't find one. Then he saw a farmer in his garden. Benny went to the farmer and said, "Excuse me, Mr. Farmer, do you have a carrot for me? I am very hungry."

The farmer said, "Yes, I have a carrot for you. But I urge you to be careful because it's very hot." Benny said, "Thank you, Mr. Farmer. I will be careful." The farmer gave Benny a big, orange carrot. Benny took a big bite and it was very delicious. He felt very happy and full.

Benny said to the farmer, "Thank you so much for the carrot. It was very kind of you." The farmer said, "You're welcome, Benny. I am happy to help a hungry rabbit." Benny said goodbye to the farmer and hopped away, feeling very content.

He saw a big ant on a leaf. He wanted to catch it. He reached out his hand and grabbed the ant. The ant bit him. It hurt a lot. Ben cried and dropped the ant.

"Stop, stop, stop!" he heard a voice. It was his mom. She came to him and saw his hand. It was red and swollen. She was angry and worried.

"Ben, why did you catch the ant? Ants are not toys. They can bite you and make you sick. You have to be careful and gentle with bugs. They are living things too. Now we have to go to the doctor. You might need medicine."

Ben felt sorry and scared. He did not want to go to the doctor. He did not want to take medicine. He wished he had not caught the ant. He wished he had listened to his mom. He learned a hard lesson.

One day, her mom took her to the theater. It was a big building with many seats and a stage. Anna was excited to see a show. She had never been to the theater before. She wondered what the show would be about.

The show was about a princess who lived in a castle. She was very rich and had many dresses and jewels. But she was not happy. She wanted to have friends and go on adventures. She met a prince who was poor but kind. He showed her the world outside the castle. They fell in love and decided to run away together.

Anna liked the show. She thought the princess and the prince were brave and sweet. She wished she could be like them. She clapped her hands and cheered when the show was over. She thanked her mom for taking her to the theater. She said it was the best day ever.

Sam and Mia liked to play with blocks. They made big towers and houses and cars with the blocks. They had many colors and shapes of blocks. They thought blocks were interesting.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a big bag of blocks. He looked sad and lonely. Sam and Mia wanted to be his friend. They went to him and said hello.

"Hi, I'm Sam. This is Mia. What's your name?" Sam asked.

"I'm Leo. I like blocks," the boy said.

"We like blocks too. Can we play with you?" Mia asked.

"OK. But be careful. These are my special blocks. They are magic," Leo said.

Sam and Mia were curious. They wanted to see the magic blocks. Leo opened his bag and showed them. The blocks were shiny and sparkly. They had strange symbols and patterns on them. They looked very interesting.

"Wow, these are cool. How are they magic?" Sam asked.

"Watch this," Leo said. He took a block and threw it in the air. The block flew like a bird and made a loud noise. Sam and Mia clapped and laughed.

"Can we try?" Mia asked.

"Sure. But only one at a time. And don't mix them up. They have to match," Leo said.

Sam and Mia each took a block and threw it in the air. The blocks flew like birds and made loud noises. They had fun with the magic blocks.

But then, something bad happened. Sam and Mia got bored of throwing the blocks. They wanted to build something with them. They took more blocks from Leo's bag and started to stack them together. They did not pay attention to the symbols and patterns. They mixed them up.

Leo saw what they were doing and got angry. He shouted at them.

"Stop! Stop! You can't do that! You're ruining my blocks! You're making them explode!"

But it was too late. The blocks that Sam and Mia stacked together started to glow and shake. They made a big boom. The blocks broke into pieces. The pieces flew everywhere. They hit Sam and Mia and Leo. They hurt them a lot. They cried and screamed.

Some people heard the noise and came to help. They saw the broken blocks and the hurt children. They called for help. They tried to rescue them.

But the blocks were too magic. They did not stop exploding. They made more booms. They broke more things. They hurt more people. They made a big mess.

Sam and Mia and Leo wished they never played with the magic blocks. They wished they listened to Leo. They wished they were safe and happy. But they were not. They were sorry and sad. The end.

Lily was a big girl who went to school. She liked to learn new things and play with her friends. But there was a boy named Tom who was not nice to her. He always said mean things and took her toys. He was ignorant. He did not know how to share or be kind.

One day, Lily had a new pencil with a pretty flower on it. She was very happy and wanted to draw with it. She put it on her desk and went to get some paper. But when she came back, her pencil was gone. She looked around and saw Tom holding it. He was laughing and breaking it. Lily felt very sad and angry.

She ran to Tom and tried to get her pencil back. But Tom was bigger and stronger. He pushed her away and threw the pencil on the floor. He said, "You are stupid and ugly. You don't deserve this pencil. It is mine now." Lily started to cry. She felt very hurt and alone.

But then, she heard a voice. It was her teacher, Miss Lee. She had seen what Tom did. She was very mad. She said, "Tom, you are in big trouble. You have been very rude and mean to Lily. You have to say sorry and give her back her pencil. And you have to go to the corner and think about what you did. You are ignorant. You need to learn how to respect and care for others."

She took Tom by the hand and made him hurry to the corner. She picked up the broken pencil and gave it to Lily. She said, "Lily, I am so sorry that Tom hurt you. You are a smart and beautiful girl. You deserve this pencil. Here, I have another one for you. It is the same as yours, but not broken. You can keep it and draw with it. And you can sit next to me and show me your pictures. I am proud of you."

Lily smiled and hugged Miss Lee. She felt very happy and grateful. She said, "Thank you, Miss Lee. You are the best teacher ever. I love you." She took the new pencil and went to sit next to Miss Lee. She drew a big heart and wrote, "Lily and Miss Lee are friends." She showed it to Miss Lee, who smiled and said, "That is a wonderful picture, Lily. You are very talented. I love you too." They hugged again and laughed. Lily forgot about Tom and his ignorance. She felt safe and loved.

"What is this, mom?" Sara asked.

"It's a cauliflower, Sara. We can break it into small pieces and cook it for dinner. It's very tasty and good for you," mom said.

Sara tried to break the cauliflower, but it was too hard. She pulled and twisted, but it did not come apart. She got frustrated and threw it on the floor. It made a loud noise and broke into many pieces.

"Oh no, Sara! What did you do?" mom said. She was not happy. She picked up the pieces and put them in the trash.

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to break it, but it was too hard. I don't like cauliflower. It's not tasty," Sara said.

Mom sighed and hugged Sara. She said, "It's okay, Sara. I know you were trying to help. But you have to be gentle with the food. And you have to try new things. Maybe you will like cauliflower if you taste it with some cheese or sauce."

Sara nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will try it next time. Can I help you with something else?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. How about you wash these carrots? They are easy to break and very tasty."

Sara was very happy today. She was going to a new classroom with new friends. She had a big backpack with her favorite books and toys. She hugged her mom and dad and said goodbye.

She walked with her teacher to the new classroom. It was very big and bright. There were many tables and chairs and a big board. There were also many pictures and colors on the walls. Sara saw some kids playing and talking. She felt a little shy.

The teacher smiled and said, "Hello, everyone. We have a new friend today. Her name is Sara. Can you say hello to Sara?" The kids said hello and smiled. Some of them waved. Sara smiled back. She felt a little better.

The teacher said, "Sara, why don't you introduce yourself to the class? You can tell us something about yourself, like what you like to do or what you brought in your backpack." Sara nodded. She walked to the front of the class. She felt a little nervous.

She said, "Hello, my name is Sara. I like to read books and play with dolls. I brought my favorite book and my favorite doll in my backpack. Do you want to see them?" The kids said yes and nodded. Sara opened her backpack and took out her book and her doll. She showed them to the class. The kids said wow and clapped. Sara felt very happy.

She did not notice that she also took out something else from her backpack. It was a small bottle of water. It was very cold. It slipped from her hand and rolled on the floor. It hit the teacher's foot and made her jump. The water spilled on the floor and made a big puddle. The kids laughed and gasped. Sara felt very embarrassed.

The teacher said, "Oh, Sara, what a surprise! You also brought a cold bottle of water. That was very funny. Don't worry, it's okay. Accidents happen. Let's clean it up together." The teacher got a mop and a towel. She helped Sara wipe the water. The kids helped too. They made a game out of it. They said sorry and thank you to the teacher. The teacher said it's all right and hugged Sara. Sara felt very relieved.

She said, "I'm sorry, teacher. I didn't mean to make a mess. I hope you're not mad at me." The teacher said, "No, Sara, I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you're here. You're a very brave and kind girl. You have a lot to share with us. You made us laugh and smile. You're a great addition to our classroom. We're happy to have you as our friend." The kids said yes and cheered. Sara felt very proud.

She said, "Thank you, teacher. Thank you, friends. I'm happy to be here too. I hope we can have more fun and learn more things together." The teacher said, "We will, Sara. We will. Welcome to our classroom." The kids said welcome and hugged Sara. Sara felt very warm. She forgot about the cold bottle of water. She remembered her favorite book and her favorite doll. She remembered her new friends and her new teacher. She remembered her big smile and her big backpack. She was very happy today. She was going to a new classroom with new friends.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play and joke with each other. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide and run to it.

Ben goes first. He slides down fast and laughs. He says, "That was fun!" Sam goes next. He slides down faster and laughs louder. He says, "That was more fun!"

They take turns to slide. Each time, they try to slide faster and louder than the other. They joke and say, "I am the best slider!" and "No, I am the best slider!"

But they are not polite. They do not wait for their turn. They do not let other kids slide. They push and shove and yell. The other kids are sad and angry. Their moms are not happy.

One time, Ben slides so fast that he falls off the slide. He hurts his knee. He cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow!" Sam slides so fast that he bumps into Ben. He hurts his head. He cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow!"

Their moms come and help them. They put band-aids on their knee and head. They say, "You were not polite. You did not share the slide. You did not joke nicely. You were rude and selfish. You made other kids and us unhappy. You also hurt yourselves. That was not fun at all."

Ben and Sam feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry. We were wrong. We will be polite. We will share the slide. We will joke nicely. We will make other kids and you happy. We will also be careful. We want to have fun, but not hurt anyone."

Their moms hug them and say, "We forgive you. We love you. We are glad you learned your lesson. Now, go and play nicely with the other kids. And remember to say please and thank you."

Ben and Sam nod and smile. They go and play nicely with the other kids. They wait for their turn. They let other kids slide. They joke and say, "You are a good slider!" and "Thank you for sliding with me!" They are polite and kind. They have fun and make friends. Their moms are proud and happy.

The moral of the story is: Be polite and share. Joke nicely and do not hurt anyone. Have fun and make others happy.

"Ow, ow, ow! Fluffy hurt me!" Anna sobbed.

Her aunt ran to her and checked her face. She saw a red mark on Anna's cheek. She took a wet cloth and cleaned it. She hugged Anna and kissed her.

"I'm sorry, Anna. Fluffy didn't mean to hurt you. He was just scared and angry. You have to be gentle with him and respect his space. Do you understand?" her aunt said.

Anna nodded. She felt sorry for Fluffy too. She looked at him and said, "I'm sorry, Fluffy. I won't move you again. Can we be friends?"

Fluffy came closer and rubbed his head against Anna's leg. He purred and licked her hand. Anna smiled and petted him. She learned her lesson. She and Fluffy became friends.

Lily and Ben got up and walked to the dog. They saw a lady holding a leash.

"Hello, can we pet your dog?" Lily asked.

"Of course, his name is Rex. He is very nice," the lady said.

Lily and Ben reached out their hands and touched Rex. He wagged his tail and licked their faces.

"He is so soft and warm!" Lily said.

"He is so cute and funny!" Ben said.

They laughed and played with Rex. They forgot about their ice cream. Their cones started to melt. The ice cream dripped on the ground.

Rex smelled the ice cream. He liked ice cream. He wanted some. He jumped and grabbed Lily's cone. He bit it and ate it. Lily screamed.

"Hey, that's mine!" Lily said.

She was angry and sad. She loved her ice cream. She wanted it back. She cried.

"Bad dog! Bad dog!" she yelled.

Rex did not understand. He thought he was good. He liked Lily. He wanted to make her happy. He licked her face.

"Stop it! Go away!" Lily said.

She pushed Rex away. Rex felt hurt. He whimpered.

The lady saw what happened. She was sorry.

"Oh, I'm so sorry. Rex didn't mean to. He just loves ice cream. Here, I'll buy you another one," she said.

She took some money and went to the truck. She came back with a new cone for Lily.

"Here you go, sweetie. I hope this makes you feel better," she said.

She gave Lily the cone. Lily took it. She looked at it. She did not want it. She threw it on the ground.

"I don't want it! I hate ice cream! I hate dogs! I hate you!" she said.

She ran to her mom and hugged her. She sobbed.

The lady was shocked. She did not know what to say. She felt bad.

"Come on, Rex. Let's go," she said.

She took Rex and left. Rex looked back at Lily. He was sad. He wanted to be her friend. He wanted to heal her hurt. He did not know how. He sighed.

It is a robot that can talk and move." Tom and Lily felt sad and angry. They loved their dollhouse and did not want Ben to make fun of it.

They said to Ben, "Our dollhouse is not silly. It is a luxury and we care for it. Your robot is not a better toy. It is loud and rude. You cannot play with our dollhouse. Go away!" Ben did not listen. He said, "I can play with whatever I want. You are just babies who do not know anything. Watch me!" He grabbed the dollhouse and lifted it up. He tried to shake it and make it fall.

Tom and Lily screamed and ran to stop Ben. They pulled the dollhouse from his hands and hugged it. They said, "Stop it, Ben! You are mean and bad. You are breaking our dollhouse. You do not care for anything. Go away and do not come back!" Ben dropped the dollhouse and ran away. He was scared and sorry. He did not mean to break the dollhouse. He just wanted to have some fun.

Tom and Lily checked their dollhouse. It was not broken, but some furniture was loose and some dolls were missing. They fixed the furniture and found the dolls. They said, "We are glad our dollhouse is okay. We are sorry Ben was mean to us. We hope he learns to care for other people's toys. We love our dollhouse and we love each other." They smiled and hugged. They played with their dollhouse and had fun.

Lila and Sam were playing dress-up in the attic. They found a big box of old clothes and hats and scarves. Lila liked a red dress with shiny buttons and a long veil that covered her face. She put it on and pretended to be a princess.

"Look at me, Sam! I am a princess and you are my knight!" she said.

Sam smiled and picked up a wooden sword and a helmet. He put them on and pretended to be a brave knight. He bowed to Lila and said, "Yes, my princess. I will protect you from the dragon!"

They ran around the attic, making noises and having fun. They saw a big stuffed animal that looked like a dragon. It had green scales and yellow eyes and a long tail. Sam pointed his sword at it and said, "There is the dragon, princess! Do not be afraid, I will fight it!"

Lila hid behind a chair and said, "Be careful, knight! The dragon is very big and scary!"

Sam ran towards the dragon and swung his sword. He hit the dragon's tail and made it fall over. He shouted, "I did it, princess! I defeated the dragon!"

Lila clapped her hands and said, "Hooray, knight! You are very strong and brave!"

She ran to Sam and gave him a hug. She lifted her veil and said, "Thank you, knight. You are my hero!"

Sam blushed and said, "You are welcome, princess. You are very beautiful and kind!"

They smiled and kissed each other on the cheek. They were very happy and proud of their adventure. They decided to keep playing dress-up until their mom called them for dinner.

"Anna, give me that red block!" Ben said. He reached for the block that Anna was holding.

"No, Ben, this is my block!" Anna said. She pulled the block away from Ben.

"Stop, Anna, this is mine!" Ben said. He held the block tight.

Anna did not listen. She pinched Ben's arm. Ben cried out. He dropped the block and rubbed his arm.

"Ow, Anna, that hurt!" Ben said. He was sad and mad.

Ben looked at the block. He looked at Anna. He smiled. He gave the block back to Anna. "No, you can have it. It's a nice block. And you are my sister."

Anna smiled too. She hugged Ben. "Thank you, Ben. You are my brother. And we can share the block."

They played with the block together. They found out that it was a light block. It made a spark when they pressed a button. They liked the spark. It was bright and pretty. They made a house with the light block on top. It was their house. And they were happy.

Lily said, "No, Tom, that is not a sword. That is a stick. A sword is shiny and sharp. A stick is brown and dull. You cannot be a knight with a stick."

Lily shook her head and said, "No, Tom, you are wrong. A sword is not like that. A sword is like this." She took a toy sword from the box and showed it to Tom. It was shiny and sharp. It had a handle and a blade. It made a sound like this: clang, clang!

Tom was angry. He said, "That is not a sword, Lily. That is a toy. A toy is not real. A toy is fake. You cannot be a knight with a toy."

"Lily and Tom, what have you done?" Mom said. "You broke the jar and wasted the cookies. You made a big mess and could have hurt yourselves. You did not listen to me. You were very naughty."

Lily and Tom felt very sorry. They wanted to say sorry to Mom, but they did not know how. They started to cry.

Lily and Tom felt very lonely and sad. They wished they had listened to Mom and played nicely. They learned that being naughty has bad consequences. They hoped Mom would forgive them and love them again.

"Let's have some cake," Sara says.

"No, we can't. Mom will be angry," Ben says.

"But I'm hungry. And the cake is yummy," Sara says.

"Mmm, so good," she says.

Ben sees Sara eating the cake. He is scared. He hears Mom coming.

"Sara, stop! Mom is here!" he says.

But Sara does not listen. She steals another piece of cake. She has cake all over her face.

Mom walks in the kitchen. She sees the cake on the shelf. She sees Sara and Ben.

"What are you doing?" she asks.

Sara and Ben look at Mom. They are quiet.

Mom sees the cake pieces in Sara's hand. She sees the cake crumbs on the floor. She is not happy.

Sara nods. She is sorry.

"Ben, did you help her?" she asks.

Ben shakes his head. He is honest.

Sara feels bad. She wants to make Mom happy.

Mom smiles. She loves Sara and Ben. She gives them a hug.

They tried to measure the things like the book said, but they did not have a cup or a spoon. They used their hands and guessed how much they needed.

"That's nice, Ben," Lily said. She was not very interested in blocks. She had an adorable bunny in her arms. She put a hat and a scarf on it. "Look, my bunny is warm and pretty!"

Ben looked at Lily's bunny. He wanted to play with it. He put down his hammer and reached for the bunny.

"Hey, that's mine!" Lily said. She pulled the bunny away from Ben. "You have your own toys!"

Ben was angry. He wanted the bunny. He grabbed his hammer and swung it at the bunny.

"Stop!" Lily shouted. She was scared. She hugged the bunny tight.

The hammer hit the bunny's hat. The hat flew off. The bunny's ears popped out. They were long and floppy.

Ben and Lily stared at the bunny. They saw its ears. They saw its face. It was not a real bunny. It was a toy bunny that could open and close its eyes.

"Wow!" Ben said. He dropped his hammer. He touched the bunny's ears. "It can open its eyes!"

"Cool!" Lily said. She smiled. She pressed the bunny's paw. The bunny made a sound. It said, "I love you!"

Ben and Lily laughed. They forgot their fight. They decided to share the bunny. They took turns holding it and making it talk. They played happily with the adorable toy bunny.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Sara was a lion and Ben was a monkey. They roared and jumped and laughed.

But soon they felt tired and hungry. Their mom came and said, "It's time for lunch and nap, my little ones. Come and eat some delicious soup and bread." Sara and Ben nodded and followed their mom to the kitchen. They liked soup and bread, especially with cheese and butter.

They sat at the table and ate their lunch. They drank some milk and said, "Thank you, mom, for the yummy food." Their mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, my sweeties. Now, let's go to your room and take a nap. You need some rest after playing so hard."

Sara and Ben went to their room and got into their beds. They had their favorite blankets and stuffed animals with them. Sara had a pink bunny and Ben had a blue bear. They hugged them and closed their eyes.

But Ben was not sleepy. He wanted to play some more. He whispered to Sara, "Hey, Sara, are you asleep?" Sara opened one eye and said, "No, Ben, I'm not asleep. But mom said we have to nap. It's the truth." Ben said, "But napping is boring. Let's play a game. I have an idea." Sara said, "What is it, Ben?" Ben said, "Let's pretend we are asleep, but we are not. We can make funny faces and noises when mom is not looking. It will be fun." Sara thought for a moment and said, "OK, Ben, let's do it. But we have to be quiet and careful. We don't want mom to find out." Ben said, "Don't worry, Sara, we are smart. Mom will never know." They giggled and agreed.

They pretended to be asleep, but they were not. They made funny faces and noises when mom was not looking. They stuck out their tongues and crossed their eyes. They snored and farted and burped. They thought it was hilarious.

But mom was not fooled. She heard their noises and saw their faces. She was not angry, but she was amused. She decided to play along. She tiptoed to their room and said, "Oh, look at my little ones. They are sleeping so peacefully. They are so cute and quiet." She kissed them on their cheeks and said, "I love you, Sara and Ben. Sweet dreams." She pretended to leave, but she stayed at the door.

Sara and Ben heard their mom and stopped their game. They felt guilty and silly. They looked at each other and said, "Oops, mom knows. We are sorry, mom. We were just playing." Mom said, "I know, my darlings. I was playing too. But now it's really time for nap. You need some rest after playing so hard." Sara and Ben said, "OK, mom. We will nap for real. We love you, mom. Good night." Mom said, "I love you too, my sweeties. Good night." She closed the door and left.

Sara and Ben snuggled with their blankets and stuffed animals. They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of lions and monkeys and soup and bread. They were happy and cozy. They napped for real.

One day, Anna saw a big flower in the garden. It was yellow and red and had many petals. She wanted to pick it and take it home. She ran to the flower and reached for it. But she felt a sharp pain in her hand. She looked and saw a bee on the flower. The bee had stung her. Anna cried and ran to her mom.

"Mom, mom, the bee hurt me!" Anna sobbed. "I wanted the flower, but the bee was mean!"

Her mom hugged her and put some ice on her hand. She said, "I'm sorry, Anna, that must have hurt a lot. But you know, the bee was not mean. The bee was just protecting the flower. The flower is the bee's home and food. The bee values the flower very much. It needs the flower to live and make honey. If you pick the flower, you take away the bee's home and food. That is not nice."

Anna looked at her mom and the flower. She felt sorry for the bee. She said, "I didn't know that, mom. I just liked the flower. But I don't want to take away the bee's home and food. I want the bee to be happy and make honey. Can I say sorry to the bee?"

You can also say thank you to the bee for making honey and pollinating the flowers. The bee helps the flowers grow and make seeds. The seeds make more flowers. The flowers make the garden beautiful and give us joy. We should value the flowers and the bees. They are both important and wonderful."

Anna nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will say sorry and thank you to the bee. And I will not pick the flowers anymore. I will just look at them and smell them and enjoy them. I will value the flowers and the bees. They are both pretty and make me happy."

Benny's friend, a kind bear named Bobby, noticed that Benny looked sad. "What's wrong, Benny?" asked Bobby. "I want to play with the animals, but I'm too shy to ask," replied Benny.

Bobby smiled and said, "Don't worry, Benny. I'll add you to the game!" Bobby went over to the animals and told them to include Benny in their game. Benny was so happy and grateful to have such a kind friend like Bobby. From that day on, Benny learned that it's okay to ask for help and that true friends will always be there for you.

The moral of the story is that sharing is important and can make everyone happy. Even if there is only one toy, you can always fold something to share with your twin.

Suddenly, she had a bright idea. She grabbed the novel and ran outside under the rain. She opened the book, and the raindrops made it wet. The girl smiled and started to read her novel. The gloomy sky seemed a bit brighter.

The girl read her novel until she couldn't read it anymore. She was happy that she could still enjoy it, even though it was raining. She ran back inside and put the wet novel down. As she looked out at the gloomy sky, she felt happy inside.

She spread out her wings and flew high up in the sky. She sang loud and happy. Row was relieved and she was so excited. As she flew, she saw something on the ground. It was a deaf kitten. 

Row swooped down and picked up the kitten. She flew back and released the kitten in the meadow. The little kitten was so happy. Row and the kitten were now friends.

Ever since then, Row and the little deaf kitten would fly through the sky and be happy together.

One morning, Jill looked out the window and observed the spring air. She could see the sun shining and the birds chirping. She smiled and was excited to explore. She grabbed her coat and went outside.

When she stepped outside, the chilly spring wind blew. She shivered and was worried. But she kept going. She saw two birds on a branch and ran to them. She listened to their chirping, she observed their feathers and she watched them hop around.

Suddenly, she heard a sound. "Chirp, chirp," it said. Jill looked around, but she couldn't see anyone. She was worried until she noticed a small voice coming from the bush. "Chirp, chirp," it said again.

Jill went over to the bush and, peeking through the leaves, saw a little baby bird. She said, "Hi little bird. Are you okay?" The little bird stopped chirping and looked at Jill with big, curious eyes. Jill smiled and said, "It must have been a scary night. Let's get you back to your family!" Together they went back to the birds Jill had spotted earlier, and soon the baby bird was back home. Jill waved goodbye and went back inside, feeling very happy.

"Why does the spaghetti attach to the pot, Mom?" Mia asked.

"Because it's sticky, Mia. It's made of flour and water. When it cooks, it becomes soft and sticky. That's why we need to stir it sometimes," Mom said.

Mom gave them a wooden spoon and let them stir the spaghetti. They had fun making bubbles and splashes. They smelled the yummy sauce that Mom was making on another stove. It had tomatoes, cheese, and meat.

"Is the spaghetti ready, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Almost, Ben. Let me check. Yes, it's ready. Let's drain the water and put the sauce on top," Mom said.

Mom poured the spaghetti into a colander and shook off the water. She put the spaghetti on a big plate and poured the sauce over it. She sprinkled some more cheese on top.

"Yummy, yummy, spaghetti!" Ben and Mia said.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in their room. They had a big bed with a soft mattress that they could jump on and make forts with. One day, they found a cheap toy wand in a box of old things. It was shiny and had a star on the end.

"Let's pretend we are magic!" Lily said. "We can make things vanish with this wand!"

"OK!" Ben said. "But be careful, don't make anything important vanish!"

They took turns waving the wand and saying "Vanish!" at different things in their room. They made a pillow, a book, a sock, and a teddy bear vanish. They laughed and clapped their hands.

Then, Lily pointed the wand at the mattress and said "Vanish!" But nothing happened. She tried again, but still nothing. She frowned and shook the wand.

"Maybe it's broken," Ben said. "Or maybe the mattress is too big to vanish."

"Let me try," Lily said. She waved the wand harder and said "Vanish!" louder. Suddenly, the mattress disappeared with a loud pop. Lily and Ben gasped and looked at the empty bed frame.

"Uh-oh," Ben said. "We made the mattress vanish!"

"What do we do?" Lily said. "Mom and Dad will be mad!"

They heard footsteps outside their door. They quickly hid the wand under the bed and pretended to be asleep on the floor.

Mom and Dad came in and saw the twins lying on the floor. They looked at the bed and saw no mattress.

"Where is the mattress?" Mom asked.

"Did you take it somewhere?" Dad asked.

Lily and Ben opened their eyes and shrugged. They didn't know how to explain what happened.

Mom and Dad looked puzzled and worried. They wondered if someone had stolen the mattress or if it had somehow fallen out of the window. They decided to call the police and ask for help.

Lily and Ben felt sorry and scared. They wished they had never played with the cheap toy wand. They hoped the mattress would come back soon. They learned a lesson: never make things vanish with magic.

Lily and her friends learned that even though something looks small and dark, it can still grow big and strong. They also learned that it's important to take care of things that are important to us, just like they took care of the bean.

Once upon a time, there was a tall giraffe named Jerry. Jerry loved to step around the grassy fields and eat leaves from the trees. One day, Jerry met a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy was looking for a match to light his fire so he could cook his dinner. 

"Hello, Jerry! Do you know where I can find a match?" asked Timmy.

"A match? Hmm, I'm not sure. Let me look around," replied Jerry.

Jerry stepped around the fields, searching for a match. Finally, he found one lying on the ground. 

"Here you go, Timmy! I found a match for you," said Jerry.

"Thank you, Jerry! You're so kind," said Timmy, lighting his fire and cooking his dinner. 

From that day on, Jerry and Timmy became good friends and would often step around the fields together, looking for more matches and having fun.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park with their toy automobiles. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. Sometimes they pretended they were driving to faraway places, like the zoo or the moon.

One day, they saw a big, shiny automobile parked near the swings. It was red and had a big bow on top. Sam and Mia ran over to look at it. They wondered who it was for.

"Maybe it's for Santa Claus," Sam said.

"Or maybe it's for a princess," Mia said.

They wanted to touch it and see inside, but they knew they had to ask first. They looked around for the owner, but they didn't see anyone.

"Hello?" Sam called out. "Can we see your automobile?"

There was no answer. Sam and Mia waited for a while, but nobody came. They started to feel curious and bored.

"Maybe they won't mind if we just peek," Mia said.

"Okay, but be careful," Sam said.

They tiptoed closer to the automobile and peeked through the window. They saw a man sitting in the driver's seat. He was wearing a suit and a hat. He looked very still and quiet.

"Hello, mister," Sam said. "Do you like your automobile?"

The man didn't move or say anything. Sam and Mia thought he was sleeping.

"Maybe we should wake him up," Mia said.

She reached out and tapped on the window. The man still didn't move or say anything.

"Maybe he's dead," Sam said.

Mia gasped. She felt scared and sad.

"What does dead mean?" she asked.

Sam shrugged. He didn't know either. He only heard the word on TV sometimes.

"I think it means he's not alive anymore," he said.

"Like a bug?" Mia asked.

"Maybe," Sam said.

They looked at the man again. He didn't look like a bug. He looked like a person, but a person who couldn't talk or play or drive.

They felt sorry for him. They wished they could help him.

"Maybe we should give him the bow," Mia said.

She took the bow from the top of the automobile and put it on the man's hat. She hoped it would make him happy.

"Bye, mister," she said. "We hope you like your bow."

Sam and Mia ran back to their toy automobiles. They decided to play somewhere else. They didn't want to bother the dead man anymore. They hoped someone would come and take care of him soon.

Sara had a bad fall from her bike. She hurt her arm and it was very sore. Mom took her to the doctor. Sara did not like the doctor. He was old and grumpy. He said she had to get an x-ray.

"What is an x-ray?" Sara asked.

"It is a picture of your bones. It will show me if your arm is broken or not," the doctor said.

Sara was scared. She did not want a picture of her bones. She thought it would hurt. She said, "No, no, no! I hate x-rays! I want to go home!"

Mom hugged Sara and said, "It's okay, sweetie. X-rays don't hurt. They are very fast and easy. They will help the doctor fix your arm. You are very brave. I will be with you the whole time."

Sara still did not want an x-ray, but she trusted Mom. She followed the doctor to a big machine. He gave her a dry gown to wear. He told her to lie down on a table and hold still. He put a heavy blanket on her chest. He said, "Don't move. I will be right back."

Sara heard a beep and saw a flash. The x-ray was done. The doctor came back and looked at a screen. He smiled and said, "Good news, Sara. Your arm is not broken. You just have a sprain. You will need a bandage and some ice, but you will be fine."

Sara was happy. She did not have a broken arm. She did not have to wear a cast. She said, "Thank you, doctor. I'm sorry I was scared. X-rays are not so bad."

The doctor said, "You're welcome, Sara. You were very brave. X-rays are nothing to be afraid of. They are very useful. They help me see what is wrong and how to help you."

Sara smiled and said, "I'm glad you can see my bones. They are very strong. They will heal fast. Can I see the picture of my bones?"

The doctor said, "Sure, Sara. Here it is. Do you see your arm bone? It is not cracked or bent. It is just a little swollen. That is why it hurts."

Sara looked at the picture of her bones. She thought it was very cool. She said, "Wow, that is my arm bone. It looks like a stick. Can I keep the picture?"

The doctor said, "Of course, Sara. You can keep the picture. It is a souvenir of your x-ray. You can show it to your friends and family. They will be proud of you."

Sara said, "Thank you, doctor. You are very nice. I don't hate x-rays anymore. I like them. They are very interesting."

Mom said, "I'm proud of you, Sara. You did a great job. You are very smart and curious. You learned something new today. Now let's go home and get some ice cream."

Sara said, "Yay, ice cream! I love ice cream. Let's go, Mom. Bye, doctor."

Mom and Sara waved goodbye to the doctor and left. Sara held her picture of her bones and her bandaged arm. She was happy. She learned that x-rays are not scary. They are helpful and cool. She did not hate them anymore. She liked them. She liked learning new things. She liked being brave. She liked ice cream. She liked Mom. She liked herself. She was a happy girl.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and smooth and had many legs.

"Hello, caterpillar," Lily said. "Do you want to be my friend?"

The caterpillar did not answer. It was busy eating the leaf.

Lily reached out her hand to touch the caterpillar. She wanted to feel how smooth it was. But the caterpillar did not like that. It curled up into a ball and made a hissing sound.

"Ow, caterpillar, you are mean!" Lily said. She felt sad and angry. She wanted to make the caterpillar be her friend.

She tried to grab the caterpillar and put it in her pocket. But the caterpillar did not want to go. It resisted. It wriggled and bit Lily's finger.

"Ouch, caterpillar, you hurt me!" Lily cried. She dropped the caterpillar and ran to her mom.

Mom saw Lily's finger. It was red and swollen. She put some ice on it and gave Lily a hug.

"What happened, Lily?" Mom asked.

"I wanted to play with a caterpillar, but it was mean and it bit me," Lily said.

Mom shook her head. "Lily, you should not touch caterpillars. They are not toys. They are living things. They have their own feelings and needs. They do not like to be bothered or moved. They need to eat and grow and change. Maybe one day, the caterpillar will become a butterfly. Then you can watch it fly and admire its colors. But you have to let it be. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She felt sorry for the caterpillar. She realized she had been wrong. She learned to respect the caterpillar and its life.

"Can I say sorry to the caterpillar?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled. "Yes, you can. But be careful. And don't touch it. Just say sorry and leave it alone."

Lily and Mom went back to the garden. They found the caterpillar on the same leaf. It was still eating.

Lily bent down and whispered. "Sorry, caterpillar. I won't bother you again. I hope you become a beautiful butterfly."

The caterpillar did not answer. But it seemed to relax a little. It uncurled and stretched its legs.

Lily and Mom walked away. They left the caterpillar in peace. They did not know that soon, the caterpillar would make a cocoon and transform. They did not know that one day, they would see a bright and smooth butterfly flying in the garden. And they did not know that the butterfly would remember Lily and her words. And it would smile.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Friends are important. Safety is important.

Anna and Ben nodded and ran to the festival. They saw many people and things. Anna wanted to go to the stage where a band was playing. Ben wanted to go to the tent where a clown was making jokes.

"Come with me, Ben," Anna said. "The music is nice and the dancing is fun."

"No, come with me, Anna," Ben said. "The clown is funny and the games are cool."

They pulled each other's hands, but they did not agree. They got angry and let go. Anna went to the stage and Ben went to the tent. They did not look at each other.

Anna enjoyed the music and the dancing. She saw many balloons and got one. It was pink and shiny. She smiled and hugged it. She looked for Ben, but she did not see him. She felt sad and lonely.

Ben enjoyed the clown and the games. He won a prize and got one. It was a toy car and it was fast. He laughed and played with it. He looked for Anna, but he did not see her. He felt bored and sorry.

They both wished they had stayed together. They both missed each other. They both wanted to say sorry.

They walked around the festival, looking for each other. They passed by many stalls and booths. They saw many things, but they did not like them. They saw a stall with food. It smelled bad and looked disgusting. They saw a stall with clothes. They were ugly and dirty. They saw a stall with animals. They were noisy and scary.

They did not want to stay at the festival. They wanted to go home. They wanted to see their mom. They wanted to see each other.

They finally found each other at the gate. They ran to each other and hugged. They said sorry and smiled. They showed each other their balloons and prizes. They liked them and shared them. They were happy and glad.

They went to their mom and told her about the festival. They told her about the music and the clown, the dancing and the games, the balloons and the prizes. They also told her about the food and the clothes, the animals and the stalls. They said they were disgusting and scary.

Mom listened and nodded. She said she was proud of them for having fun and for making up. She said she loved them and hugged them. She said it was time to go home.

Anna and Ben agreed. They said goodbye to the festival and got in the car. They held each other's hands and closed their eyes. They dreamed of the next festival they would go to together. They dreamed of the nice and fun things they would see and do. They dreamed of being twins and being friends.

One day, they were playing in the backyard. Sara was the driver and Ben was the doctor. They had a teddy bear as their patient. Sara drove the box around the grass and made noises like an ambulance. Ben checked the teddy bear's ears and paws and gave it a band-aid. He used the toy phone to tell the hospital they were coming.

But Sara was restless. She wanted to go faster and faster. She did not listen to Ben when he said to be careful. She drove the box over a bump and it tipped over. Sara and Ben and the teddy bear fell out. Sara hit her head on a rock and started to cry. Ben was scared. He dropped the toy phone and ran to get their mom.

Mom came and saw Sara's head. It was bleeding. She hugged Sara and Ben and told them to stay calm. She used her real phone to call a real ambulance. She said they had to go to the hospital. Sara and Ben were both very quiet. They did not want to play pretend anymore.

Soon, they heard a loud noise. It was the real ambulance. It had a red cross and lights and sirens. It looked like their box, but bigger and shinier. Two people came out. They were real doctors. They had a stretcher and a bag of tools. They talked to mom and looked at Sara's head. They put a bandage on it and lifted her onto the stretcher. They told Ben to come with them. They said they would take good care of Sara.

Ben held mom's hand and followed the doctors. He looked at the ambulance. He saw his and Sara's box next to it. It was broken and dirty. He felt sad and sorry. He wished he could repeat the day and play nicer with Sara. He hoped she would be okay. He got into the ambulance with mom and Sara. The doors closed and the ambulance drove away.

"Let's go inside, Ben. The storm is scary," Lily said.

"No, I want to stay and watch the lightning. It is cool and pretty," Ben said. He did not listen to his sister.

Lily ran inside the house and told their mom about the storm. Mom said they should stay safe and warm until the storm was over. She gave Lily a cup of hot chocolate and a book to read.

Ben stayed outside and watched the lightning. He saw a big tree near the fence. The tree had many apples that looked red and juicy. Ben wanted to pick some apples and eat them. He ran to the tree and climbed on a branch.

But the branch was old and weak. It had rot inside and could not hold Ben's weight. The branch broke and Ben fell to the ground. He hurt his arm and his leg. He cried and called for help.

Lily heard Ben's cry and ran outside with Mom. They saw Ben lying on the ground near the tree. Mom picked him up and took him inside. She cleaned his wounds and put a bandage on them. She said he was lucky that the lightning did not hit him or the tree.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was silly and did not listen to Lily. I wanted to see the lightning and eat the apples," Ben said.

"It's okay, Ben. I'm glad you are not badly hurt. But you should always listen to your sister and me when we tell you to do something. We want you to be safe and happy. And you should not eat apples from a rotten tree. They are not good for you. They can make you sick," Mom said.

"I know, Mom. I learned my lesson. I will listen to you and Lily next time. And I will not eat rotten apples. I will eat fresh ones from the market," Ben said.

Lily hugged Ben and said, "I'm happy you are okay, Ben. I love you, brother. You are my best friend."

"I love you too, Lily. You are my best friend too," Ben said.

They smiled and drank their hot chocolate. They watched the storm pass and the sun come out. They learned that listening to each other and being careful was better than being curious and reckless. They also learned that rotten things were not good for them. They wanted to be healthy and strong. They were happy and grateful for their family.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Daisy and Bobby. Every day, they would have playtime together. They would run around and hug each other and giggle.

One day they came to the park and Daisy saw something that made her happy. She saw a beautiful dancer! Daisy asked Bobby, "Can I talk to the dancer?"

But Bobby said, "No! You don't even know her. Let's go have fun somewhere else"

But Daisy was so excited that she had already started to walk towards the dancer. Bobby ran after her, but she had already reached the dancer and asked, "Can I kiss you?"

The dancer was taken by surprise. She looked down at Daisy and said, "No, I don't think that would be a good idea."

Daisy was a bit sad, but she wasn't hungry so she didn't mind too much. Just then, Bobby came to Daisy's rescue. He said, "Let's go get something to eat. We can buy food from the food truck over there and then go back to playing!"

The moral of this story is to not be so quick to talk to strangers. It's always important to ask for permission first, and in this case, it was safest not to kiss the dancer. Always learn to be polite and kind, even when you're feeling excited or hungry.

Once upon a time, there was a very hungry bear. He was so hungry that he was looking for something to eat.
He saw a little bird on a tree, and called out to her, "Can you help me? I am so hungry!"

The bird looked down and said, "I'm sorry, but I don't have any food. Why don't you try climbing a tree, and see if you can find something to eat up there?"

The bear climbed up the tree, and sure enough, he found a scale. He grabbed it in his big paw, and was so happy. He said to the little bird, "Thank you! Now I can eat this scale, and then I won't be so hungry anymore!"

The bird was happy too. She asked, "Do you want me to write you a note, to thank you for helping me when I was hungry?". The bear said yes, and the bird wrote him a thank you note.

When the bear was finished eating the scale, he thanked the bird for the note, and said goodbye. He left with a full tummy, feeling much less hungry.

Johnny flew down and settled on the ground next to the hare. Together they watched the sun turn the valley a deep red. Then the stars began to twinkle in the night sky. 

Johnny felt something he had never felt before, a feeling of peace and harmony. He thanked the hare and flew home happy.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly lady who lived in a small cottage. She loved to bake pies and cakes, but she always had trouble measuring the ingredients. One day, she decided to ask her neighbor, a young girl named Lily, for help with measuring.

Lily was happy to help and showed the elderly lady how to use a measuring cup. The lady was grateful and promised to bake a pie for Lily as a thank you. 

As the days went by, the leaves on the trees began to change color and fall to the ground. The lady remembered her promise to bake a pie for Lily, but she didn't have any apples left. She decided to take a walk to the nearby orchard to pick some fresh apples.

On her way to the orchard, the lady slipped on a fallen leaf and hurt her ankle. She couldn't walk anymore, but luckily Lily came by and helped her. The lady was grateful for Lily's help once again and decided to make her a special apple pie with the fresh apples she had picked. 

In the end, the lady and Lily enjoyed the delicious pie together, and the lady learned a valuable lesson about measuring and the importance of having good neighbors.

They swam closer to the plant. It looked ugly and smelled bad. They saw something moving under the leaves. It was a big snake!

"Ah, a snake!" Ben shouted. "Swim away, Mia, swim away!"

They turned around and swam as fast as they could. The snake followed them, hissing and snapping. They reached the shore and ran to their house.

"Mom, Dad, there's a snake in the pond!" they cried.

Their parents came out and looked at the pond. They saw the snake and the plant.

"That's not a plant, that's a water hyacinth. It's an invasive weed that can harm the pond and the animals. And that's a water moccasin, a venomous snake that can bite you. You were very lucky to escape," their dad said.

"We're sorry, we didn't know. We won't swim in the pond anymore," Ben and Mia said.

Their mom hugged them and said, "It's OK, you're safe now. But next time, don't touch anything you don't recognize in the water. And always swim with a grown-up nearby."

Ben and Mia nodded and said, "Yes, mom."

They learned their lesson and never swam in the pond again. They found other ways to have fun in the summer.

"Is it ready, mother?" Lily asked.

"Not yet, my love. We have to wait for the pasta to boil. Then we can pour the sauce over it and bake it in the oven. It will be hot and bubbly and delicious," her mother said.

Lily nodded. She was patient. She knew her mother would tell her when it was ready. She trusted her mother. She was reliable. She always kept her promises.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the zoo with his mom and dad. He liked to see all the animals, but his favorite was the monkey. He wanted to get closer to the monkey, so he wandered away from his mom and dad. He did not see the sign that said "Do not feed the animals".

He found a banana in his pocket and threw it to the monkey. The monkey was happy and caught the banana. He peeled it and ate it. Then he saw Tom and smiled. He wanted to play with Tom, so he jumped off the tree and ran to him.

"Hi, monkey!" Tom said. "Do you want to be my friend?"

The monkey nodded and made a funny noise. He grabbed Tom's hand and pulled him to the fence. He wanted to show Tom his home.

But Tom's mom and dad were looking for him. They were worried and scared. They asked the zookeeper if he had seen Tom. The zookeeper said he had seen a boy with a monkey.

They ran to the monkey cage and saw Tom and the monkey. They were glad and relieved. They called Tom's name and told him to come back.

"Tom, come here!" his mom said. "You should not wander away from us. It is not safe. And you should not feed the animals. It is not good for them."

"Sorry, mom," Tom said. "But the monkey is nice. He is my friend."

The monkey waved goodbye to Tom and went back to his tree. He was sad, but he understood. He hoped to see Tom again.

Tom hugged his mom and dad and said he was sorry. He learned his lesson. He said goodbye to the monkey and thanked him for the banana. He left the zoo with his mom and dad. He was happy, but he was also slow. He was tired from his adventure.

Tommy was a little boy who liked to eat a lot of candy. He always asked his mom for more candy, even when she said no. He did not like to eat healthy food, like fruits and vegetables. He only wanted sweet things.

One day, his mom went to the store and left Tommy with his dad. Tommy saw his chance to get more candy. He ran to the kitchen and opened the refrigerator. He saw a big bowl of candy on the top shelf. He reached for it, but it was too high. He got a chair and climbed on it. He grabbed the bowl and smiled.

But then he heard his dad's voice. "Tommy, what are you doing?" his dad asked. He came into the kitchen and saw Tommy with the candy. He was not happy. "Tommy, you know you are not supposed to eat candy before dinner. Put it back in the refrigerator, please."

Tommy refused. He held the bowl tightly and said, "No, I want candy. It is mine. Go away." He stuck out his tongue at his dad.

His dad was very angry. He took the bowl from Tommy and put it back in the refrigerator. He said, "Tommy, you are being very rude and selfish. Candy is not good for you. It can make you sick and hurt your teeth. You need to eat healthy food to grow strong and smart. And you need to listen to your parents and be respectful. If you don't, you will have no candy at all, and you will have a time out."

Tommy felt bad. He realized he had made a mistake. He said, "I'm sorry, dad. I was wrong. I don't want to be sick or hurt my teeth. I don't want to be rude or selfish. I want to be good and nice. Can I have some fruit instead of candy?"

His dad smiled and hugged him. He said, "That's better, Tommy. I'm glad you understand. Yes, you can have some fruit. And maybe later, you can have a little candy as a treat, if you eat your dinner and behave well."

Tommy nodded and smiled. He learned his lesson. He decided to eat healthy food and be polite. He knew that candy was not everything, and that his dad loved him.

The moral of the story is: Don't eat too much candy, and listen to your parents.

But then they heard a loud voice. It was a man who was sitting on the bench. He was angry. He had a hat and a shirt that matched the sign.

"Hey, you kids, what are you doing?" he shouted. "That's my lemonade. I'm selling it for a dollar a cup. You owe me money. Give me back my cups."
